2.7.m: Now begins the māhātmya of the month of Vaiśākha.
Having bowed down to Nārāyaṇa, and to Nara, the foremost among men,
and to the goddess Sarasvatī, and to Vyāsa, one should then proclaim the triumph. (1)
Sūta said:
Once again the king questioned Nārada, the son born of the limbs
of Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, about the holy māhātmya of Mādhava. (1)
Ambarīṣa said:
"The māhātmya of all the months has indeed been heard

2.7.s: śrutaṃ mayā purā brahmanyadā coktaṃ tadā tvayā .. 2 ..
2.7.d: श्रुतं मया पुरा ब्रह्मन्यदा चोक्तं तदा त्वया .. 2 ..
2.7.m: from you by me previously, O brahmin, whenever it was spoken by you then. (2)
'Vaiśākha is undoubtedly the foremost among these months'—
thus [it was said]. Therefore, there is curiosity to hear in detail the māhātmya of Mādhava, (3)
O brahmin: How is this [month] dear to Viṣṇu?

2.7.s: ke ca viṣṇupriyā dharmā māse mādhavavallabhe .. 4 ..
2.7.d: के च विष्णुप्रिया धर्मा मासे माधववल्लभे .. 4 ..
2.7.m: And what are the duties dear to Viṣṇu in the month beloved of Mādhava? (4)

2.7.s: tatrāpyasya tu kartavyāḥ ke dharmā viṣṇuvallabhāḥ ..
2.7.d: तत्राप्यस्य तु कर्तव्याः के धर्मा विष्णुवल्लभाः ..
2.7.m: And what duties dear to Viṣṇu are to be performed in it by a person?

2.7.s: kiṃ dānaṃ kiṃ phalaṃ tasya kamuddiśyā''caredimān .. .. 5 ..
2.7.d: किं दानं किं फलं तस्य कमुद्दिश्या'ऽचरेदिमान् .. .. 5 ..
2.7.m: What is the gift? What is its fruit? For whose sake should one observe these? (5)
With what substances should that Mādhava be worshipped at the arrival of the month of Mādhava?
O Nārada, explain this in detail to me who am endowed with faith." (6)
The venerable Nārada said:
"Formerly, Brahmā was questioned by me concerning the ancient duties of the months.
He related what was previously declared to Śrī by the Supreme Self. (7)

2.7.s: tato māsā viśiṣyoktāḥ kārtiko māgha eva ca ..
2.7.d: ततो मासा विशिष्योक्ताः कार्तिको माघ एव च ..
2.7.m: Then, among the months, Kārtika and Māgha were mentioned as distinguished;
among them, Mādhava made Vaiśākha the best of months. (8)
Like a mother to all living beings, it is always the granter of desires,
destroying all sins by means of gifts, sacrifices, vows, and ritual ablutions. (9)
It is the essence of religious duties and sacrificial rites, the essence of austerity, worshipped by the gods.
Just as the knowledge of the Vedas is among forms of knowledge, just as the praṇava is among mantras, (10)
just as the tree of the gods is among trees, just as the wish-yielding cow is among cows,
just as Śeṣa is among all serpents, just as Garuḍa is among birds, (11)

2.7.s: devānāṃ tu yathā viṣṇurvarṇānāṃ brāhmaṇo yathā ..
2.7.d: देवानां तु यथा विष्णुर्वर्णानां ब्राह्मणो यथा ..
2.7.m: just as Viṣṇu is among gods, just as a brahmin is among castes,
just as the vital breath is among dear things, just as a wife is among friends, (12)

2.7.s: āpagānāṃ yathā gaṃgā tejasāṃ tu raviryathā ..
2.7.d: आपगानां यथा गंगा तेजसां तु रविर्यथा ..
2.7.m: just as the Gaṅgā is among rivers, just as the sun is among lights,

2.7.s: āyudhānāṃ yathā cakraṃ dhātūnāṃ kāṃcanaṃ yathā .. 13 ..
2.7.d: आयुधानां यथा चक्रं धातूनां कांचनं यथा .. 13 ..
2.7.m: just as the discus is among weapons, just as gold is among metals, (13)

2.7.s: vaiṣṇavānāṃ yathā rudro ratnānāṃ kaustubho yathā ..
2.7.d: वैष्णवानां यथा रुद्रो रत्नानां कौस्तुभो यथा ..
2.7.m: just as Rudra is among Vaiṣṇavas, just as the Kaustubha is among gems,
so also is Vaiśākha the best among the months that cause religious merit. (14)
There is nothing equal to it in the world that brings about the delight of Viṣṇu.
When the sun is in Aries, toward one engaged in ritual ablution in Vaiśākha before the rising of the sun, (15)
the Lord accompanied by Lakṣmī shows abundant affection.
Just as the satisfaction of living beings is indeed produced by food alone, (16)
in the same way, Viṣṇu is undoubtedly pleased by ritual ablution in Vaiśākha.
Seeing people devoted to ritual ablution in Vaiśākha, he rejoices; (17)
by that alone, freed from sins, one is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
Having bathed even once in the morning when the sun is in Aries and having performed the daily rites, (18)
freed from great sins, that person attains liberation by merging into Viṣṇu.
If one takes even a single step for the sake of ritual ablution in the month of Vaiśākha, (19)
he undoubtedly attains the fruit of ten thousand horse sacrifices.
Even if one with a deceitful mind merely forms the mental resolve [to bathe], (20)

2.7.s: so'pi kratuśataṃ puṇyaṃ labhedeva na saṃśayaḥ ..
2.7.d: सोऽपि क्रतुशतं पुण्यं लभेदेव न संशयः ..
2.7.m: even he certainly obtains the religious merit of a hundred sacrifices; there is no doubt.
Whoever walks the length of a bow to bathe while the sun is in Aries
is freed from all bonds and attains intimate union with Viṣṇu.
Whatever sacred fords there are in the three worlds and within the cosmic egg,

2.7.s: tāni sarvāṇi rājendra saṃti bāhye'lpake jale ..
2.7.d: तानि सर्वाणि राजेन्द्र संति बाह्येऽल्पके जले ..
2.7.m: all of them, O king of kings, are present in any outdoor puddle of water.
Recorded sins roar in the judgment hall of Yama
only until a creature performs a ritual ablution in water in the month of Vaiśākha.
All the deities presiding over sacred fords, O king,
resort to outdoor water and remain present at all times, O king.
Beginning with sunrise, up to the end of six ghaṭikās,
they remain by order of Viṣṇu, desiring the welfare of men.
To men who have not arrived by that time, they utter a terrible curse
and return to their own abodes, O king of kings; therefore one should perform a ritual ablution.

2.7.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe vaiśākhamāsamāhātmye nāradāmbarīṣasaṃvāde vaiśākhamāsa praśaṃsāpūrvaka vaiśākhasnānamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 1 ..
2.7.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे वैशाखमासमाहात्म्ये नारदाम्बरीषसंवादे वैशाखमास प्रशंसापूर्वक वैशाखस्नानमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः .. 1 ..
2.7.m: Thus ends the first chapter, named 'The Description of the Māhātmya of Vaiśākha Ablution, Preceded by the Praise of the Month of Vaiśākha', in the dialogue between Nārada and Ambarīṣa, in the Vaiśākhamāsamāhātmya of the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.
Nārada said:

2.7.s: na mādhavasamo māso na kṛtena yugaṃ samam ..
2.7.d: न माधवसमो मासो न कृतेन युगं समम् ..
2.7.m: There is no month equal to Mādhava; there is no yuga equal to Kṛta;

2.7.s: na ca vedasamaṃ śāstraṃ na tīrthaṃ gaṃgayā samam .. 1 ..
2.7.d: न च वेदसमं शास्त्रं न तीर्थं गंगया समम् .. 1 ..
2.7.m: there is no scripture equal to the Veda; there is no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā.

2.7.s: na jalena samaṃ dānaṃ na sukhaṃ bhāryayā samam ..
2.7.d: न जलेन समं दानं न सुखं भार्यया समम् ..
2.7.m: There is no gift equal to water; there is no happiness equal to a wife;

2.7.s: na kṛṣestu samaṃ vittaṃ na lābho jīvitātparaḥ .. 2 ..
2.7.d: न कृषेस्तु समं वित्तं न लाभो जीवितात्परः .. 2 ..
2.7.m: there is no wealth equal to agriculture; there is no gain higher than life.
There is no austerity equal to fasting; there is no supreme happiness other than giving;

2.7.s: na dharmastu dayātulyo na jyotiścakṣuṣā samam.. 3 ..
2.7.d: न धर्मस्तु दयातुल्यो न ज्योतिश्चक्षुषा समम्.. 3 ..
2.7.m: there is no righteousness equal to compassion; there is no light equal to the eye.

2.7.s: na tṛptiraśanāttulyā na vāṇijyaṃ kṛṣeḥ samam ..
2.7.d: न तृप्तिरशनात्तुल्या न वाणिज्यं कृषेः समम् ..
2.7.m: There is no satisfaction equal to food; there is no trade equal to agriculture;

2.7.s: na dharmeṇa samaṃ mitraṃ na satyena samaṃ yaśaḥ .. 4 ..
2.7.d: न धर्मेण समं मित्रं न सत्येन समं यशः .. 4 ..
2.7.m: there is no friend equal to righteousness; there is no fame equal to truth.
There is no rising equal to good health; there is no protector higher than Keśava;

2.7.s: na mādhavasamaṃ loke pavitraṃ kavayo viduḥ .. 5 ..
2.7.d: न माधवसमं लोके पवित्रं कवयो विदुः .. 5 ..
2.7.m: the wise know nothing in the world as purifying as the month of Mādhava.
Mādhava is the supreme month, ever dear to the one who reclines on Śeṣa.
Whoever passes the month dear to Mādhava without vows
promptly enters an animal womb, excluded from all righteousness.
For those mortal beings whose Mādhava passes without vows,
their sacrificial rites and public works are in vain, O best among upholders of dharma.
When a restriction is made in Mādhava concerning customary foods,
one certainly attains intimate union with Viṣṇu; of this there is no doubt.
In this world there are diverse vows requiring vast wealth,
which merely cause bodily exertion and grant yet another rebirth;
by a ritual ablution in Vaiśākha alone, one is not born again on earth.
Whatever merit is in all gifts, whatever fruit is in all sacred fords,
that fruit one attains completely from the gift of water in Mādhava.
One incapable of giving water, if desirous of prosperity,
should awaken others to do so—a beneficial deed surpassing all gifts.
All gifts placed on one side, and the gift of water on the other,
were formerly weighed in the balance: the gift of water proved superior.

2.7.s: mārge'dhvagānāṃ yo martyaḥ prapādānaṃ karoti hi..
2.7.d: मार्गेऽध्वगानां यो मर्त्यः प्रपादानं करोति हि..
2.7.m: Whatever mortal provides a water-booth on the road for travellers
delivers ten million members of his lineage and is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.

2.7.s: devānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ca ṛṣīṇāṃ rājasattama..
2.7.d: देवानां च पितॄणां च ऋषीणां राजसत्तम..
2.7.m: For the gods, the ancestors, and the seers, O best of kings,

2.7.s: atyaṃta prītidaṃ satyaṃ prapādānaṃ na saṃśayaḥ.. 15..
2.7.d: अत्यंत प्रीतिदं सत्यं प्रपादानं न संशयः.. 15..
2.7.m: the gift of a water-booth truly brings supreme delight; there is no doubt.
The one by whom those exhausted from the fatigue of travel are gratified through the gift of a water-booth,
by him the gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest—are pleased.
Water to those desiring water, an umbrella to those desiring shade,
a fan to those desiring a fan in the month of Vaiśākha, O king—

2.7.s: jalaṃ chatraṃ ca vyajanaṃ dānaṃ yeṣāṃ viśiṣyate ..
2.7.d: जलं छत्रं च व्यजनं दानं येषां विशिष्यते ..
2.7.m: the gift of these: water, an umbrella, and a fan, is superior.
When the month of Mādhava has arrived, [if one lives] without giving to a householder brahmin
a water pot, he is reborn on earth as a cātaka bird.
Whoever gives cool water to an exalted soul tormented by thirst
attains by that alone, O king of kings, [the fruit of] ten thousand Rājasūya sacrifices.
Whoever fans with a fan a brahmin afflicted by the fatigue of heat
becomes free of sin by that alone and becomes king of the birds.

2.7.s: adattvā vyajanaṃ bhūpa vaiśākhe tu dvijātaye ..
2.7.d: अदत्त्वा व्यजनं भूप वैशाखे तु द्विजातये ..
2.7.m: Without giving a fan to a twice-born in Vaiśākha, O king,
one is beset with a hundred wind-diseases and finds only hells.
Whoever fans an eminent twice-born weary on the road, even with a cloth,
is thereby liberated and attains intimate union with Viṣṇu.
Whoever, having given a palm-leaf fan with a pure mind...
shaking off all sins, he goes to the world of Brahmā. // 24

2.7.s: sadyaḥ śramaharaṃ puṇyaṃ na dadyādvyajanaṃ naraḥ..
2.7.d: सद्यः श्रमहरं पुण्यं न दद्याद्व्यजनं नरः..
2.7.m: If a man does not give a fan, which instantly dispels fatigue and brings merit,

2.7.s: nārakīṃ yātanāṃ bhuktvā kaśmalo jāyate bhuvi.. 25..
2.7.d: नारकीं यातनां भुक्त्वा कश्मलो जायते भुवि.. 25..
2.7.m: he suffers the torments of hell and is born on earth as a foul creature. // 25
For the pacification of afflictions, beginning with the personal ones, O lord of men,
one who makes a home should diligently give an umbrella in the month of Vaiśākha. // 26
A man who gives no umbrella in Vaiśākha, the month beloved of Mādhava,
is born on earth as a shadowless, exceedingly cruel piśāca. // 27
He who gives a pair of divine sandals in [the month of] Mādhava, beloved of Mādhava,
spurns the two messengers of Yama and goes to the world of Viṣṇu. // 28
He who gives footwear upon the arrival of Vaiśākha, the month of Mādhava,

2.7.s: na tasya nārako loko na kleśā aihikāśca ye ..29..
2.7.d: न तस्य नारको लोको न क्लेशा ऐहिकाश्च ये ..29..
2.7.m: has no hellish world [to face], nor any earthly afflictions. // 29
He who gives sandals to a begging brahmin
becomes a king on earth for ten million births; of this there is no doubt. // 2.7.2.30
He who erects a rest-pavilion on the road that relieves weariness,

2.7.s: tasya puṇyaphalaṃ vaktuṃ brahmaṇā'pi na śakyate ..31..
2.7.d: तस्य पुण्यफलं वक्तुं ब्रह्मणाऽपि न शक्यते ..31..
2.7.m: even Brahmā cannot describe the fruit of his merit. // 31
If he feeds a brahmin guest who has arrived at midday,
even Brahmā has not fully defined the resting-place of that fruit. // 32
The gift of food brings immediate satisfaction to mortals, O king;
therefore, no gift equal to food exists in the worlds. // 33
He who provides shelter to a brahmin exhausted from the road,

2.7.s: tasya puṇyaphalaṃ vaktuṃ brahmaṇā'pi na śakyate .. .. 34 ..
2.7.d: तस्य पुण्यफलं वक्तुं ब्रह्मणाऽपि न शक्यते .. .. 34 ..
2.7.m: even Brahmā is unable to declare the fruit of his merit. // 34
Wife, offspring, house, and the rest; clothing, adornments, and ornaments—

2.7.s: asahyaṃ nāśnataḥ puṃsaḥ sahyaṃ bhuktavato dhruvam .. 35 ..
2.7.d: असह्यं नाश्नतः पुंसः सह्यं भुक्तवतो ध्रुवम् .. 35 ..
2.7.m: for a man who does not eat, these are intolerable; for one who has eaten, they are surely enjoyable. // 35

2.7.s: tasmādannasamaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati ..
2.7.d: तस्मादन्नसमं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति ..
2.7.m: Therefore, a gift equal to food has never been nor will ever be.

2.7.s: vaiśākhe yena cādattaṃ mārgaśrāṃte ca bhūsure..36..
2.7.d: वैशाखे येन चादत्तं मार्गश्रांते च भूसुरे..36..
2.7.m: If someone does not give [it] in Vaiśākha to a brahmin exhausted from the road,
he becomes a piśāca on earth and eats only his own flesh.
Therefore, food should be given to a twice-born according to one's means. // 37
The giver of food makes one forget mother, father, and other kin, O king;
therefore, the people dwelling in the three worlds praise food. // 38
Mothers and fathers are merely the causes of birth,

2.7.s: annadaṃ pitaraṃ loke vadanti ca manīṣiṇaḥ ..39..
2.7.d: अन्नदं पितरं लोके वदन्ति च मनीषिणः ..39..
2.7.m: and the wise call the giver of food the [true] father in this world. // 39
All sacred fords abide in the giver of food; all deities abide in the giver of food;
and all dharmas reside in the giver of food, O conqueror of enemy kings! // 2.7.2.40

2.7.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe vaiśākhamāsamāhātmye nāradāmbarīṣasaṃvāde dānanirūpaṇaṃnāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ .. 2 ..
2.7.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे वैशाखमासमाहात्म्ये नारदाम्बरीषसंवादे दाननिरूपणंनाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः .. 2 ..
2.7.m: Thus ends the second chapter, named 'Description of Gifts', in the praise of the month of Vaiśākha, in the dialogue between Nārada and Ambarīṣa, in the second [book], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. // 2
Nārada said:

2.7.s: yo martyo dvijavaryāya paryaṃkaṃ tu dadāti hi ..
2.7.d: यो मर्त्यो द्विजवर्याय पर्यंकं तु ददाति हि ..
2.7.m: The mortal who gives a couch to the best of the twice-born,
whereon he sleeps at ease, in comfort, fanned by cool breezes, // 1
and obtains freedom from disease in his body, which is the instrument of dharma—

2.7.s: taṃ dattvā sakalaṃ tāpaṃ nirasya gatakalmaṣaḥ .. 2 ..
2.7.d: तं दत्त्वा सकलं तापं निरस्य गतकल्मषः .. 2 ..
2.7.m: having given that, casting off all torment, cleansed of taint, // 2
he goes to the unbroken state, difficult of attainment even for yogins.
To the twice-born who are afflicted by the summer heat and exhausted in Vaiśākha, // 3
by giving a splendid couch that dispels fatigue, O lord of men,
he never languishes in the world through birth, death, old age, and the rest. // 4
Where a brahmin, having received it, lies down and dwells for life,
when he is seated [there], all the sin committed knowingly or unknowingly // 5

2.7.s: vilayaṃ yāti rājeṃdra karpūra iva cāgninā ..
2.7.d: विलयं याति राजेंद्र कर्पूर इव चाग्निना ..
2.7.m: melts away, O king of kings, just as camphor melts with fire.

2.7.s: śayane brahmanirvāṇaṃ sa naro yāti niścitam .. 6 ..
2.7.d: शयने ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं स नरो याति निश्चितम् .. 6 ..
2.7.m: Through that bed, that man surely attains the extinction that is Brahman. // 6
He who gives a mattress in the month of Vaiśākha, beloved for ritual ablutions,
endowed with all enjoyments in that very birth, // 7
truly lives along with his lineage unsmitten by diseases and the like.

2.7.s: āyuṣyaṃ paramārogyaṃ yaśo dhairyaṃ ca viṃdati .. 8 ..
2.7.d: आयुष्यं परमारोग्यं यशो धैर्यं च विंदति .. 8 ..
2.7.m: He gains longevity, supreme health, fame, and steadfastness. // 8
For a hundred generations, no unrighteous person is born in his family.
Having enjoyed all pleasures, he then meets dissolution in death. // 9

2.7.s:
nirdhūtākhilapāpastu brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati .. śro
triyāya dvijeṃdrāya yo dadyādupabarhaṇam .. 2.7.3.10 ..
2.7.d:
निर्धूताखिलपापस्तु ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति .. श्रो
त्रियाय द्विजेंद्राय यो दद्यादुपबर्हणम् .. 2.7.3.10 ..
2.7.m: His every sin shaken off, he attains the extinction that is Brahman. / He who gives a pillow to a learned brahmin, steeped in scripture, // 2.7.3.10

2.7.s: sukhaṃ nidrā vinā yena na nṛṇāṃ jāyate kvacit ..
2.7.d: सुखं निद्रा विना येन न नृणां जायते क्वचित् ..
2.7.m: without which pleasant sleep never comes to mortals anywhere,

Ambarīṣa said:
Vaiśākha is superior to all dharmas and to the dharmas of austerity.
How did it become greater than all months and even greater than gifts? (1)
Nārada said:
I shall explain that, O wise one; listen with single-minded attention.
At the end of a kalpa, Viṣṇu, the king of gods and supreme lord who reclines upon Śeṣa, (2)
holding this multitude of worlds within his belly, sleeps upon the ocean of dissolution,
having attained unity, though manifold, through his manifestations by means of yogamāyā. (3)
At the conclusion of a twinkling of an eye, however, he was awakened by the Vedic scriptures;
then that ocean of compassion protected the multitudes of living beings resting within his belly. (4)
In order that they might attain the fruits of their respective actions, he set his mind on producing creation.
From his navel arose a golden lotus, the resting-place of the worlds. (5)
He brought forth Brahmā, the cosmic being named Puruṣa;
in him the Lord created the fourteen worlds, (6)
and the many diverse multitudes of living creatures possessing different karmic residues,
as well as the material nature endowed with the three qualities, the bounds of conduct in the world, and the guardians. (7)
He established the divisions of caste and life-stage and the ordination of dharma,
along with the four Vedas, the Tantras, and likewise the Smṛtis, (8)
and the Purāṇas and the epics, which have the nature of his own command.
The supreme sovereign, the great lord, appointed the seers as promulgators for the protection of dharma. (9)
All the subjects placed their faith in the dharmas promulgated by them,
which arose from the divisions of caste and stage of life, were suitable for themselves, and brought satisfaction to Viṣṇu. (10)
In order to behold them carrying out their duties in their respective stages of life, the Lord,
though residing within the heart, the imperishable one, for the purpose of inspection by direct test, [thought:] (11)
“The subjects perform auspicious and flawless dharmas here;
what season could that be, O wise one?” Thus the Lord pondered: (12)

Nārada said:
O king, one who does not give water in Vaiśākha to those afflicted by thirst and exhausted on the road
enters the womb of an animal.
In this connection they cite this ancient legend,
the exceedingly wondrous conversation between a brahmin and a house-lizard.
Formerly, in the lineage of Ikṣvāku, there was a king named Hemāṅga,
devoted to brahmins, generous, conqueror of his enemies, with his senses conquered.
As many as are the particles of earth, as many as are the drops of water,
as many as are the stars in the sky—just so many cows he gave away.
By him the beautiful earth was covered with kusa-grass from celebrated sacrifices;
many brahmins were satisfied with gifts of cows, land, sesame, gold, and other riches.

2.7.m: Service to great men is indeed the cause of the aims of human life.

2.7.m: When the ritual ablution performed on a single day was given by the brahmin,

Having enjoyed great pleasures there without weariness for ten thousand years,
he was born in the lineage of Ikṣvāku as Kakutstha, the great lord,
protector of the earth possessing seven continents, devoted to brahmins, approved by the virtuous,
friend of the lord of gods, a portion of Viṣṇu himself, a great ruler.
Instructed by Vasiṣṭha, having observed all the delightful religious duties

having attained divine knowledge, he achieved union with Viṣṇu.

2.7.d: पित्रा'ऽदिष्टः कृतयात्रः स्वगेहे प्राप्याऽकरं माधवे चाऽन्नदानम् ..42..
2.7.m: Instructed by my father, having completed the pilgrimage, having reached my own home, / I performed the gift of food in the month of Mādhava.

2.7.s: tasmānmukto matpitā māṃ sametya yānārūḍho hyabhinaṃdyā''śiṣā ca ..
2.7.d: तस्मान्मुक्तो मत्पिता मां समेत्य यानारूढो ह्यभिनंद्या'ऽशिषा च ..
2.7.m: Liberated by that, my father approached me, / mounted upon an aerial chariot, having congratulated me with blessings;

2.7.s: gato lokaṃ śrīpaterdurvibhāvyaṃ yasmingatā na nivartaṃti bhūyaḥ ..43..
2.7.d: गतो लोकं श्रीपतेर्दुर्विभाव्यं यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तंति भूयः ..43..
2.7.m: he went to the realm of the consort of Śrī, unfathomable, / going to which they do not return again.

2.7.s: tasmāddānaṃ sarvaśāstreṣu coktaṃ tubhyaṃ proktaṃ dharmasāraṃ sudharmyam ..
2.7.d: तस्माद्दानं सर्वशास्त्रेषु चोक्तं तुभ्यं प्रोक्तं धर्मसारं सुधर्म्यम् ..
2.7.m: Therefore, the gift [of food] has been praised in all the scriptures; / to you has been proclaimed the essence of righteousness, which is wholly righteous.

2.7.s: kimanyatte śrotumicchā vadasva śrutvā sarvaṃ te vadāmīti satyam .. 44 ..
2.7.d: किमन्यत्ते श्रोतुमिच्छा वदस्व श्रुत्वा सर्वं ते वदामीति सत्यम् .. 44 ..
2.7.m: What else do you desire to hear? Tell [me]; / having heard, I will tell you everything truly."

2.7.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe vaiśākhamāsamāhātmye nāradāmbarīṣasaṃvāde piśācamokṣaprāptirnāma saptamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 7 ..
2.7.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे वैशाखमासमाहात्म्ये नारदाम्बरीषसंवादे पिशाचमोक्षप्राप्तिर्नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः .. 7 ..
2.7.m: Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'Attainment of Liberation for the Piśāca', in the dialogue between Nārada and Ambarīṣa, in the glorification of the month of Vaiśākha, in the second Vaiṣṇava section of the venerable Skanda Purāṇa, in the compilation of eighty-one thousand [verses].

2.7.m: The King of Mithilā said: / O brahmin, the son of Ikṣvāku, through not giving water, / became a cātaka bird three times, and then a lizard in my house. / This corresponds to his karma, and is fitting for that unrefined soul. / But that through not serving the good he incurred the state of a vulture and a dog / seven times, as was stated—that does not seem right to me. / He did not revile the virtuous, nor the wretched either; / therefore, from mere non-service, absence of fruit would surely result, / not [a punishment], since in the absence of committing wrongdoing this would be inflicting injury on another. / For what causeless reason did he obtain this degraded birth? / Therefore, dispel this doubt of your disciple, who is dear to yourself. / Thus questioned well by the king, the highly renowned Śrutadeva / said, "Well spoken, well spoken!" and proceeded to utter these words: / Śrutadeva said: / Listen, O king, I shall explain what has been asked by you, O sinless one, / as was spoken by Śiva to Śivā on the spotless peak of Kailāsa: / Having created all these worlds, he then arranged their maintenance / in two ways: concerning the other world and concerning this world. / The great Lord arranged three causes for each maintenance: / service of water, service of food, and service of medicine— / where these are found, O highly fortunate one, they are the causes for maintenance in this world. / Likewise for the other world, O king, only three are proclaimed in the Veda: / service of the virtuous, service of Viṣṇu, and service of the path of dharma. / These, performed previously, are the causes of the next world, / just as provisions prepared at home serve for the journey. / The causes belonging to this world, O king, grant their objects immediately upon being performed. / Moreover, even what is desirable to the virtuous, if it is unbearable to the mind / for some reason, O king, turns out to lead to misfortune. / What need is there to speak of what is displeasing? Clearly, it is a cause of suffering. / In this very connection, they relate this ancient narrative, / which destroys sins, is a great wonder, and causes the hair to stand on end for those who hear it: / Long ago, Dakṣa Prajāpati, having undertaken initiation for a sacrifice, / went to the silver mountain to invite the Lord of Spirits. / Seeing him, Śambhu did not rise, wishing only his welfare [thinking]: / "I am the preceptor of all immortals, accessible through the Vedas, eternal. / These rulers of the gods, such as the Moon and Indra, are servants who bring offerings. / A master should not rise for a servant, nor a husband for his wife; / a teacher should not rise for a disciple: such is the opinion of those who know the scriptures. / Mere relationship is not the reason for being a guru, so says the Veda; / where strength, knowledge, austerity, and tranquility are greater, / he is the guru of the others, and the inferior should become servants. / If out of stubbornness masters and the like rise for servants and the like, / their life, wealth, and fame are ruined, and their progeny perishes immediately. / Therefore, I shall not rise, though this father-in-law is dear to me." / Seeking his welfare thus, the all-pervading Lord did not stir from his seat. / But seeing Mṛḍa not rising, Prajāpati became enraged. / He reviled him in many ways in front of the Lord of Girijā: / "Oh, the arrogance, oh, the arrogance of this impoverished, unrefined fellow! / Whose only wealth is an aged bull that is nothing but skin. / For this very reason he bears skulls and bones, moving in the realm of heretics! / Whence will destiny grant auspiciousness to a vainly conceited person? / The wise know that deeds in the world are pure by their proper performance. / Destitute and afflicted with cold, he wears a sacred elephant's skin; / his dwelling is a cremation ground, and serpents are indeed his adornment! / There is no courage, nor even knowledge, in one who fled from that wolf [asura]! / He is perpetually united with wicked beings: bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, and the like. / No noble family is heard of anywhere, nor is he approved by the virtuous! / Formerly, I was falsely made to place trust by the wicked Nārada, / by whom I was persuaded and gave him this Satī, my daughter. / Following a different code of conduct, let her dwell happily in his house! / He is not to be praised by us, nor my daughter in any way, / like a potter's jar that has fallen into the power of an outcaste!" / Thus Dakṣa, foolish in mind, without inviting Umā or that Mṛḍa, / having severely rebuked him, went home in silence. / Then, going to the sacrificial arena together with the priests and sages, / he sacrificed according to the rite, constantly reviling the great Lord. / Leaving aside Brahmā and Viṣṇu, all the gods assembled: / the siddhas, cāraṇas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kinnaras. / Then the virtuous goddess Satī, enticed by womanly fickleness, / was eager to see the festival and the relatives gathered there. / Being restrained by Rudra, unsteady due to woman's nature, / though answered again and again, she resolved: "I must go!" / [Śiva said:] "He always insults me in the midst of the assembly, O fair-complexioned one; / and hearing that unbearable [insult], you will truly abandon your body. / Even what is unbearable must be tolerated by me, who desires a household. / As I have acted, O goddess, you do not behave at all.

Though advised thus, the goddess again became fickle.
Satī departed from the house, alone and on foot.
Seeing her, the bull silently carried the goddess upon his back.
And millions of hosts of spirits then followed Satī.
Having reached the sacrificial arena, she first went to the hall of the wife.
[Her mother] remained silent upon seeing Satī; out of distress, she went out from there.
Remembering the words of her husband, she went to the northern altar.
Seeing her, her father and the members of the assembly stood silent, their blessings destroyed.
Observing her father's conduct up to the time of the oblation to Rudra,
as he made offerings omitting Rudra, she spoke, her eyes filled with tears.
The goddess said:
Transgression of the great generally does not lead to welfare for men.
He is the creator of the worlds, the supporter of the worlds, the imperishable Lord of all.
How is sacrificial oblation not given to such a Rudra?
Do the others who have assembled not remove this wicked intent that has arisen in you?

2.7.m:
Are these great-souled ones not so? Why is fate opposed to them?
While she was speaking thus, the god Pūṣan laughed out loud;
Bhṛgu, whose auspiciousness was ruined, stroked his beard in like manner.
Others slapped their arms, feet, thighs, and armpits;
and her ill-fated father reviled [Śiva] in manifold ways.
Hearing that, she, the wife of Rudra, her mind agitated with rage,
cast off her body to perform an expiation for what was heard—she, Satī,
in the sacrificial fire in the middle of the altar, while everyone was looking on.
A great wailing arose, and the pramathas ran swiftly;
they reported the whole matter to the god of gods then.
Hearing that, rising up suddenly, Rudra, like Kāla the destroyer,
tore out a matted lock with his hand and struck it upon the ground.
From that arose Vīrabhadra of colossal body and immense strength;
he had a thousand arms, shining with a radiance like Kāla the destroyer.
Having folded his hands in reverence, he then spoke to Hara:
“For whatever purpose my creation was made by you, assign me to that purpose.”

Addressed thus, enraged Dhūrjaṭi said to him standing before him:
“Slay Dakṣa the reviler, on whose account my beloved was destroyed!
Let the hosts of spirits of mighty power go along with him.”
Commanded thus by the Lord, they then went to the sacrificial assembly;
the great heroes struck down all—gods, asuras, humans, and the rest.
And he who was born of the matted lock shattered the teeth of the laughing Pūṣan;
he plucked out the beard of that evil-minded Bhṛgu.
Whatever limb had previously been slapped, that the valiant one cut off;
then he made great effort to take Dakṣa's head.
Protected by the sages' mantras, he could not cut it off by force;
knowing this, Hara came in person and cut off [the head] of the evil-minded one.
Having thus slain those at the sacrifice, he went to his own abode with his followers.
Certain survivors went to Brahmā for refuge.
Accompanied by them, Brahmā went to Kailāsa, the abode of Śiva.
Then, having conciliated Rudra with diverse words,

the great lord went along with him to the sacrificial enclosure;
he revived all those who had assembled for the sacrifice.
Śiva then gave a goat's face to Dakṣa for his fame;
and Śambhu gave a goat's beard to the great-souled Bhṛgu.
He did not give Pūṣan his teeth back, making him an eater of ground flour;

Having undertaken lifelong celibacy, Rudra of great tapas
practiced austerity on the bank of the Gaṅgā, seated at the root of a punnāga tree.

was born to Menakā from the Himālaya, and grew up in his house.

2.7.m:
chose the boon of invulnerability to gods, asuras, humans, and serpents,
and to all weapons and missiles of great power.
“O daitya, you shall indeed be invulnerable to all, except for a son of Rudra”—
thus Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, granted him the boon,
saying “So be it,” because Rudra had no wife and had no son.
Having obtained the boon and returned to his home, he oppressed the worlds:
the gods were servants for sweeping and such, and the goddesses were servant-maids in his house.
Then, afflicted by him, the gods went to Brahmā for refuge;
hearing their affliction described by them, the Creator said this to the gods:
“O gods, at the time of granting the boon, except for a son of Rudra,
I granted the boon to that evil-minded one that he cannot be slain at all.
Formerly, Satī, the wife of Rudra, abandoned her body at the sacrificial session;
was born as the daughter of Himavat, whom they know as Pārvatī. (74b)
Rudra performs severe austerity on the ridge of Himavat.
Unite Rudra, the lord of the worlds, the master, with Pārvatī!" (75)

2.7.m:
Then, having assembled again in the dwelling of Devendra with the chiefs of the immortals,
and having deliberated also with Dhiṣaṇa, Devendra, the chastiser of Pāka, (76)
remembered Nārada and Smara as well, for the sake of the task.
Then, when the two arrived there, the slayer of Bala spoke these words: (77)
"You, sir, go to Himavat and instruct him with words:
'Your daughter was formerly the virtuous daughter of Dakṣa, the wife of Hara. (78)
Separated from [her], [Hara] performs austerity on your peak with ten maidens.
Direct his beloved to the service of Mṛḍa. (79)
She alone will be his wife; he alone will be her husband.'"
Being thus instructed by Maghavat, Nārada approached that mountain, (80)
and brought it about precisely as had been stated by Devendra.
Afterwards, having summoned Kāma, Maghavat said this to him: (81)
"For the benefit of the gods and also for the benefit of Mṛḍa,
go to the penance grove of Rudra accompanied by Spring. (82)
Manifesting the qualities of spring that bring about desire in the heart,
when the goddess Pārvatī is near Mṛḍa, (83)

2.7.m:
then, discharging your arrows, enchant the great lord.
When their union takes place, our task will indeed be accomplished." (84)
Thus instructed, Smara promptly set out, saying, "Certainly!"
Together with Spring, with Rati, and with his attendants, he went to that forest. (85)
Having unfolded the spring season out of season by his own power
in that forest, delightful on all sides and frequented by gentle breezes, (86)
at one time the god of gods, pleased by Pārvatī's service,
placed her on his lap and began to say something. (87)
Thinking, "This is the determined time for the union of the beloved of life,"
he stood behind Hara taking up his charming bow. (88)
Making a tree his screen, he released an arrow.
Fitting a second one as well, he made a great effort to loose it. (89)
Then Mṛḍa, his mind disturbed, was seized with reflection:
"My mind never wavers anywhere; by whom has it been defiled?" (90)
Thus troubled with thought, he saw Kāma on his left side.

2.7.m:
Angered, opening his forehead eye and setting the goddess down from his lap, (91)
from that eye arose a fierce fire terrifying the worlds.
By it, Manmatha together with his bow was instantly burnt. (92)
And seeing the success of their purpose, the immortals fled to heaven;
dreading their own punishment, Spring and Rati also [fled]. (93)
Closing her eyes in fear, the goddess fled far away.
To remove the presence of a woman, Mṛḍa also vanished. (94)
A god who performs what is dear to Rudra and beneficial to the mind,
incurred misfortune without end; what then for one who does what is displeasing? (95)
Therefore, the son of Ikṣvāku was always unpleasant to virtuous people;
therefore, dull-witted, he did not perform service to the good which brings benefit to oneself. (96)
Great suffering was experienced, and therefore an evil rebirth.
Therefore, one should perform service to the virtuous, which achieves all ends. (97)
Because he acted displeasingly toward Rudra, Smara, in a future birth,
experienced abundant suffering at the time of his birth, though a great lord. (98)

2.7.m: She plunged into the heavenly river, performed all the necessary rites,
restrained the collection of her senses, placed her mind firmly upon the Self,
and began to mount the funeral pyre. Then a bodiless voice arose:
“Do not enter the fire, auspicious lady, devoted as you are to your husband!
Your husband will have two births in succession,
from Hara and then from the Yādava Viṣṇu. There, in the latter birth,
he will be born of Kṛṣṇa, the Great Viṣṇu, through the daughter of Bhīṣmaka, named Pradyumna.
And you, through the curse of Brahmā, will dwell in Śambara's abode,
and you will be united with your husband named Pradyumna.”
Having spoken thus, the voice resounding in the sky fell silent.
Having heard it, though resolved upon death, she turned back.

accompanied by Lakṣmī and attended by followers, mounted on Garuḍa,
gazing upon that unbearable radiance, he immediately closed his eyes;
leaping up and falling down in joy, wandering like one intoxicated or mad,
all his limbs bristling with hair standing on end, his eyes filled with flowing tears,

2.7.m: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, named 'The Description of the Attainment of Victory and the Destruction of Poverty by the Ruler of the Pāñcāla Country,' in the dialogue between Nārada and Ambarīṣa, in the Greatness of the Month of Vaiśākha, in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the compilation of eighty-one thousand verses. 15.
Śrutadeva said:
His heart flooded with joy at that darśana, he quickly rose and bowed with his head,
having long gazed with agitated eyes upon this god who is the Self of all, the Lord of the worlds. 1.
Having washed his feet, he took that water, the river born from whose feet purifies the world up to Brahmā;
he worshiped [him] with great opulences—with precious garments, ornaments, and unguents, 2.
with garlands, incense, lamps, nectarous food, and the like, through the surrender of skin, body, wealth, and self.

2.7.s: tuṣṭāva viṣṇuṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ nirguṇamadvitīyam .. 3 ..
2.7.d: तुष्टाव विष्णुं पुरुषं पुराणं नारायणं निर्गुणमद्वितीयम् .. 3 ..
2.7.m: He praised Viṣṇu, the primordial Person, Nārāyaṇa, devoid of qualities, without a second: 3.
'I bow to the untainted supreme Lord of the creators of the universe, praised by the lotus-born [Brahmā] and others,
by whose māyā even men supreme among the knowers of truth are deluded regarding the sovereign Lord of the universe's creators. 4.

2.7.s: muhyaṃti māyācariteṣu mūḍhā guṇeṣu citraṃ bhagavadviceṣṭitam ..

2.7.m: Fools are bewildered by the acts of māyā, by the qualities—wondrous is the activity of the Blessed Lord!

2.7.s: anīha etadbahudhaika ātmanā sṛjatyavatyatti na sajjate'pyatha .. 5 ..
2.7.d: अनीह एतद्बहुधैक आत्मना सृजत्यवत्यत्ति न सज्जतेऽप्यथ .. 5 ..
2.7.m: Desireless, as the one Self, he creates, protects, and consumes this [universe] in many ways, yet is not attached. 5.
Although your desires are fulfilled, [you act] for the acquisition of pleasure and pain by all gods and asuras;

2.7.s: tatrā'pi kāle svajanābhiguptyai bibharṣi sattvaṃ khalanigrahāya .. 6 ..
2.7.d: तत्राऽपि काले स्वजनाभिगुप्त्यै बिभर्षि सत्त्वं खलनिग्रहाय .. 6 ..
2.7.m: even then, at proper time, for the protection of your own people and the restraint of the wicked, you assume sattva. 6.

2.7.s: tamoguṇaṃ rākṣasa bandhanāya rajoguṇaṃ nirguṇa viśvamūrte ..
2.7.d: तमोगुणं राक्षस बन्धनाय रजोगुणं निर्गुण विश्वमूर्ते ..
2.7.m: You assume the quality of tamas to bind the rākṣasas, and the quality of rajas, O quality-less one, whose form is the universe!

2.7.s: diṣṭyā tvadaṃghriḥ praṇatāghanāśanastīrthāspadaṃ hṛdi dhṛtaḥ suvipakvayogaiḥ .. 7 ..
2.7.d: दिष्ट्या त्वदंघ्रिः प्रणताघनाशनस्तीर्थास्पदं हृदि धृतः सुविपक्वयोगैः .. 7 ..
2.7.m: By good fortune, your foot, destroying the sins of those bowed down and the abode of sacred fords, is held in the heart by those of fully matured yoga. 7.

2.7.s: utsiktabhaktyupahṛtāśaya jīvabhāvāḥ prāpurgatiṃ tava padasmṛtimātrato ye ..
2.7.d: उत्सिक्तभक्त्युपहृताशय जीवभावाः प्रापुर्गतिं तव पदस्मृतिमात्रतो ये ..
2.7.m: Those whose sense of individual soul and desires are surrendered through overflowing devotion attained the supreme goal merely by the remembrance of your feet.
Bound by the noose-like serpent of Time called worldly existence, by the sufferings of repeated birth, old age, and the rest, 8.
I wander among wombs like mouse food, with increased craving, because of forgetting your feet.

2.7.s: nūnaṃ na dattaṃ na ca te kathā śrutā na sādhavo jātu mayā'pi sevitāḥ .. 9 ..
2.7.d: नूनं न दत्तं न च ते कथा श्रुता न साधवो जातु मयाऽपि सेविताः .. 9 ..
2.7.m: Surely, I gave no gift, nor heard your story, nor were virtuous people ever served by me. 9.
Therefore, my supreme fortune destroyed by enemies, I entered the forest, remembering my own heavy sin;

2.7.s: smṛtau ca tau māṃ samupetya duḥkhātsaṃbodhayāṃcakraturārtabaṃdhū .. 2.7.16.10 ..
2.7.d: स्मृतौ च तौ मां समुपेत्य दुःखात्संबोधयांचक्रतुरार्तबंधू .. 2.7.16.10 ..
2.7.m: and when remembered, those two kinsmen of the afflicted approached me and awakened me from sorrow, 10.
by means of the auspicious duties of Vaiśākha ordained by the Vedas, which are the causes of the human aims such as heaven and liberation.
From their instruction, I performed all those auspicious duties of the month of Mādhava; 11.

2.7.s: tasmādabhūnme paramaḥ prasādastenākhilāḥ saṃpada ūrjitā imāḥ ..
2.7.d: तस्मादभून्मे परमः प्रसादस्तेनाखिलाः संपद ऊर्जिता इमाः ..
2.7.m: therefore, your supreme grace was granted to me, and through it, all these abundant fortunes [were attained].

2.7.s: nāgnirna sūryo na ca candratārakā na bhūrjalaṃ khaṃ śvasano'tha vāṅmanaḥ .. 12 ..
2.7.d: नाग्निर्न सूर्यो न च चन्द्रतारका न भूर्जलं खं श्वसनोऽथ वाङ्मनः .. 12 ..
2.7.m: Neither fire, nor the sun, nor the moon and stars, nor earth, water, space, wind, or speech and mind, 12.
even when worshiped, remove sin except after a long time; [yet] the wise destroy it through service for a single moment—
those whom you regard as worldly beings, but who have renounced desires, their minds fixed upon your feet. 13.

2.7.s: namaḥ svataṃtrāya vicitrakarmaṇe namaḥ parasmai sadanugrahāya ..
2.7.d: नमः स्वतंत्राय विचित्रकर्मणे नमः परस्मै सदनुग्रहाय ..
2.7.m: Homage to the independent one of wondrous deeds! Homage to the supreme one of true compassion!
Deluded by your māyā among the qualities in the forms of wife and wealth, I wander, perceiving what is worthless.' 14.
Even while your lotus foot exists, which destroys the root [of ignorance] and takes away all sin, extremely pure,
bound by a sense of mineness to children, self, and wife—the very sources of calamity—out of desire for pleasure,

2.7.s: na kvāpi nidrāṃ labhate na śarma pravṛddhatarṣaḥ punareva tasmin ..
2.7.d: न क्वापि निद्रां लभते न शर्म प्रवृद्धतर्षः पुनरेव तस्मिन् ..
2.7.m: one finds no sleep anywhere, nor peace; with thirst grown ever greater, toward that very thing again,

2.7.s: labdhvā durāpaṃ naradevajanma tvaṃ yatnataḥ sarvapumarthahetuḥ ..16..
2.7.d: लब्ध्वा दुरापं नरदेवजन्म त्वं यत्नतः सर्वपुमर्थहेतुः ..16..
2.7.m: having attained this human and royal birth, so difficult to obtain, which with effort is the cause of all human goals,

2.7.s: padāravindaṃ na bhajāmi deva saṃmūḍhacetā viṣayeṣu lālasaḥ ..
2.7.d: पदारविन्दं न भजामि देव संमूढचेता विषयेषु लालसः ..
2.7.m: I do not worship your lotus foot, O God, my mind completely deluded, greedy for sense-objects.
I perform actions firmly established [in desire], my thirst grown strong, giving [gifts only] with expectation of reward,
with my mind agitated by hundreds of anxieties: 'Let me be [prosperous] again! Let me be [rich] today!'

2.7.s: tadaiva jīvasya bhavetkṛpā vibho duraṃtaśaktestava viśvamūrte .. 18 ..
2.7.d: तदैव जीवस्य भवेत्कृपा विभो दुरंतशक्तेस्तव विश्वमूर्ते .. 18 ..
2.7.m: Only then does the living being receive your grace, O omnipresent Lord of endless power, whose form is the universe,

2.7.s: samāgamaḥ syānmahatāṃ hi puṃsāṃ bhavāṃbudhiryena hi goṣpadāyate ..
2.7.d: समागमः स्यान्महतां हि पुंसां भवांबुधिर्येन हि गोष्पदायते ..
2.7.m: when there is the association of great men, by which the ocean of worldly existence becomes like a puddle in a cow's footprint.

2.7.s: satsaṃgamo deva yadaiva bhūyāttarhīśa deve tvayi jāyate matiḥ ..19..
2.7.d: सत्संगमो देव यदैव भूयात्तर्हीश देवे त्वयि जायते मतिः ..19..
2.7.m: O God, only whenever there is the company of the virtuous, then, O Lord, does the mind turn toward you, the Lord of gods.

2.7.s: samastarājyāpagamaṃ hi manye hyanugrahaṃ te mayi jātamañjasā ..
2.7.d: समस्तराज्यापगमं हि मन्ये ह्यनुग्रहं ते मयि जातमञ्जसा ..
2.7.m: Truly I consider the loss of my entire kingdom to be your grace directly manifested upon me,
just as [it was shown], O noble one, to flocks of ascetics, who have turned away their thirst, along with Brahmā, the gods, the asuras, and the rest.

2.7.s: itaḥ smarāmyacyutameva sādaraṃ bhavāpahaṃ pādasaroruhaṃ vibho ..
2.7.d: इतः स्मराम्यच्युतमेव सादरं भवापहं पादसरोरुहं विभो ..
2.7.m: Henceforth I remember with reverence only Acyuta, the lotus foot that removes worldly existence, O Lord;
sought by the possessionless, conferring immense good fortune, I desire nothing other than your lotus foot.

2.7.s: ato na rājyaṃ na sutādikośaṃ dehena śaśvatpatatā rajobhuvā ..
2.7.d: अतो न राज्यं न सुतादिकोशं देहेन शश्वत्पतता रजोभुवा ..
2.7.m: Therefore [I desire] neither kingship, nor the treasury of sons and the rest; with this body born of rajas, constantly falling,
I constantly worship that which is to be served, the lotus foot to be contemplated by sages.

2.7.s: prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa smṛtiryathā syāttava pādapadme ..
2.7.d: प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास स्मृतिर्यथा स्यात्तव पादपद्मे ..
2.7.m: Be gracious, O Lord of gods, dwelling place of the universe, so that my remembrance may rest upon your lotus foot!

2.7.s: saktiḥ sadā gacchatu dārakośaputrātmacihneṣu gaṇeṣu me prabho.. 23 ..
2.7.d: सक्तिः सदा गच्छतु दारकोशपुत्रात्मचिह्नेषु गणेषु मे प्रभो.. 23 ..
2.7.m: May my attachment always depart from wife, treasury, sons, body, status, and retinue, O Lord!
May my mind abide in the two lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, and my words in describing your divine narrative;

2.7.s: netre mameme tava vigrahekṣaṇe śrotre kathāyāṃ rasanā tadarpite .. 24 ..
2.7.d: नेत्रे ममेमे तव विग्रहेक्षणे श्रोत्रे कथायां रसना तदर्पिते .. 24 ..
2.7.m: may these two eyes of mine be [fixed] on seeing your form, my two ears on your narrative, and my tongue on what is offered to you;
and my sense of smell on the fragrance of your lotus feet and, constantly, on the anointing perfumes of your devotees;

2.7.s: syātāṃ ca hastau tava mandire vibho saṃmārjjanādau mama nityadaiva .. 25 ..
2.7.d: स्यातां च हस्तौ तव मन्दिरे विभो संमार्ज्जनादौ मम नित्यदैव .. 25 ..
2.7.m: and may my two hands always be engaged in sweeping and other services in your temple, O Lord;

2.7.s: pādau vibho kṣetrakathā'nusarpaṇe mūrdhā ca me syāttava vandane'niśam ..
2.7.d: पादौ विभो क्षेत्रकथाऽनुसर्पणे मूर्धा च मे स्यात्तव वन्दनेऽनिशम् ..
2.7.m: my two feet, O Lord, in wandering to your sacred fields and listening to your stories; and my head continuously in bowing to you;

2.7.s: kāmaśca me syāttava satkathāyāṃ buddhiśca me syāttava ciṃtane'niśam .. 26 ..
2.7.d: कामश्च मे स्यात्तव सत्कथायां बुद्धिश्च मे स्यात्तव चिंतनेऽनिशम् .. 26 ..
2.7.m: and may my desire be for your holy narrative, and my intellect continuously in meditating upon you;
may my days be spent listening to the rising of your holy narratives sung by sages who have come to my home;

2.7.s: hīnaḥ prasaṃgastava me na bhūyātkṣaṇaṃ nimeṣārddhamathā'pi viṣṇo .. 27 ..
2.7.d: हीनः प्रसंगस्तव मे न भूयात्क्षणं निमेषार्द्धमथाऽपि विष्णो .. 27 ..
2.7.m: and may my discourse never be devoid of you for even a moment or half the blink of an eye, O Viṣṇu!

2.7.s: na pārameṣṭhyaṃ na ca sārvabhaumaṃ na cāpavargaṃ spṛhayāmi viṣṇo ..
2.7.d: न पारमेष्ठ्यं न च सार्वभौमं न चापवर्गं स्पृहयामि विष्णो ..
2.7.m: I do not desire the station of Brahmā, nor universal sovereignty, nor even liberation, O Viṣṇu;

2.7.s: tvatpādasevāṃ ca sadaiva kāmaye prārthyāṃ śriyā brahmabhavādibhiḥ suraiḥ .. 28 ..
2.7.d: त्वत्पादसेवां च सदैव कामये प्रार्थ्यां श्रिया ब्रह्मभवादिभिः सुरैः .. 28 ..
2.7.m: I only ever desire service to your feet, which is prayed for by Lakṣmī, and by gods such as Brahmā and Śiva.

2.7.s: iti rājñā stuto viṣṇuḥ prasannaḥ kamalekṣaṇaḥ ..
2.7.d: इति राज्ञा स्तुतो विष्णुः प्रसन्नः कमलेक्षणः ..
2.7.m: Praised thus by the king, the lotus-eyed Viṣṇu was pleased,
and spoke to that lord of the earth with a voice deep as thunder:
The Blessed Lord said:
I know you to be the best of my servants, free from desire and without blemish.
Even so, I will grant you a boon difficult for deities to obtain:
A lifespan of ten thousand celestial [years], and riches, O ruler of men;
may your devotion to me be firm, and in the end, complete union [with me].

2.7.s: tvayā kṛtena stotreṇa māṃ stuvanti ca ye bhuvi ..
2.7.d: त्वया कृतेन स्तोत्रेण मां स्तुवन्ति च ये भुवि ..
2.7.m: And those on earth who praise me with the hymn composed by you,

2.7.s: teṣāṃ tuṣṭaḥ pradāsyāmi bhuktiṃ muktiṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 32 ..
2.7.d: तेषां तुष्टः प्रदास्यामि भुक्तिं मुक्तिं न संशयः .. 32 ..
2.7.m: to them, being pleased, I will bestow enjoyment and liberation, without doubt.
This third lunar day will be renowned on earth by the name Akṣayā,
upon which, pleased with you, I bestow the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.

2.7.s: ye kurvaṃti narā mūḍhāḥ snānadānādikāḥ kriyā ..
2.7.d: ये कुर्वंति नरा मूढाः स्नानदानादिकाः क्रिया ..
2.7.m: Those men, even if foolish, who perform rites such as ritual ablution and gift-giving,
even under a pretext or by natural inclination, go to my imperishable abode.
And those humans who, on Akṣayatṛtīyā, for the sake of the ancestors,

2.7.s: śrāddhaṃ kurvaṃti teṣāṃ vai tadānaṃtyāya kalpate .. 35 ..
2.7.d: श्राद्धं कुर्वंति तेषां वै तदानंत्याय कल्पते .. 35 ..
2.7.m: perform a śrāddha, for them indeed it becomes inexhaustible.

2.7.s: na cānayā tithirloke samā vā nādhikā bhuvi..
2.7.d: न चानया तिथिर्लोके समा वा नाधिका भुवि..
2.7.m: There is no lunar day in the world equal to or superior to this on earth;
even a very small [act] performed on this day yields an imperishable fruit.
Whoever gives a cow, O best of kings, to a householder brahmin,
enjoyment and liberation, called the downpour of all prosperity, are held in his hand.
Whoever gives a bull that destroys all sins,
being freed from untimely death, attains a long life.
Whoever performs the religious duties pleasing to me in the month of Vaiśākha,
their sin and their fear of death, old age, and birth, I take away.
Just as I am pleased by all the duties of Vaiśākha,

2.7.s: māsadharmairna tuṣṭaḥ syāṃ māso me mādhavaḥ priyaḥ .. .. 2.7.16.40 ..
2.7.m: I am not pleased by the duties of any [other] month; the month of Mādhava is dear to me.
Even if abandoned by all duties, or devoid of celibacy,
those devoted to the month of Vaiśākha go to my imperishable abode.
That which is hard to obtain through austerities, Sāṃkhya, Yoga, or even sacrifices,
to that supreme abode go the men devoted to Vaiśākha.
Even a thousand sins this month removes, O sinless one,
even without expiation, just like the remembrance of my feet.
Instructed by your guru in the forest, you have become devoted to Vaiśākha.
Having worshiped the Lord of the Universe, everything was obtained by you through that, O king!
Pleased by this practice, I have become visible to you.
Having enjoyed desires at will, difficult to attain even for the gods,

2.7.s: iti tasmai varaṃ dattvā devadevo janārdanaḥ ..
2.7.d: इति तस्मै वरं दत्त्वा देवदेवो जनार्दनः ..
2.7.m: Having thus granted a boon to him, Janārdana, the god of gods,
vanished right there, even while everyone was watching.
Then that best of kings was filled with great astonishment.
His body cheerful and thriving, O king, like one who has regained lost wealth,
then he ruled the earth, his mind fixed on him, wholly devoted to him,
constantly instructed by the great ones and perpetually by his teachers.
The king considered none dearer than Vāsudeva;
wife, ministers, sons, and others were dear only through connection with him.
He repeatedly performed all the religious duties enjoined for Vaiśākha;
by the power of that merit, surrounded by sons, grandsons, and others,
having enjoyed all desires, difficult to attain even for the gods,
he attained in the end union with God Viṣṇu, wielder of the discus.

2.7.s: ya idaṃ paramākhyānaṃ śṛṇvanti śrāvayaṃti ca ..
2.7.d: य इदं परमाख्यानं शृण्वन्ति श्रावयंति च ..
2.7.m: Those who hear and cause this supreme narrative to be heard,

2.7.s: te sarve pāpanirmuktā yāṃti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam ..52..
2.7.d: ते सर्वे पापनिर्मुक्ता यांति विष्णोः परं पदम् ..52..

2.7.m:
The story of Vālmīki's previous birth.

The hunter said:
“I have been favored by you, O sage—I, a sinner of extremely wicked mind.
For the great are naturally compassionate, the virtuous indeed so. / 1
Where is a hunter of low birth like me, and where such an intellect?
I consider this merely your supreme grace. / 2
Now, O virtuous one, I am your pupil, a fit recipient of your mercy, O honor-giver.
I am worthy of grace, I am your son; bestow your compassion, O ocean of mercy! / 3
So that such an evil mind, which brings disaster, may not arise in me again.
For through association with the good, one never again experiences sorrow. / 4
Therefore instruct me, O brahmin, with those well-spoken words that remove sin,
by which seekers of liberation truly cross the ocean of worldly existence. / 5
For the virtuous, whose minds are impartial and who have compassion for all living beings,
no one is low or high, nor is anyone their own or another. / 6
Having pondered with one-pointed focus, he who inquires about purity of heart—
whether he is full of all faults or bereft of all religious duty— / 7
whenever he asks teachers, having felt genuine remorse,
they straightaway instruct him in the knowledge that liberates from worldly existence. / 8
Just as the Gaṅgā is destined to destroy the sins of men,
so the virtuous are known to have the nature of uplifting the lowly. / 9
Do not hesitate to enlighten me, O compassionate one, affectionate to devotees,
because of my desire to serve, my submission, and the purity arising from your company.” / 10

Having heard this speech of the hunter, his mind amazed once more,
addressing him with “Well done! Well done!”, he spoke of these religious duties: / 11

Śaṅkha said:
“Perform the divine duties pleasing to Viṣṇu that grant liberation from the ocean of worldly existence
in the month of Vaiśākha, O hunter, if you desire welfare. / 12
Terrible heat oppresses us, and there is neither shade nor water here.
Therefore let us go to another place where there is shade. / 13
Having gone there, drunk water, and resorted to pleasant shade,
I shall describe to you the sin-destroying māhātmya / 14
of Viṣṇu, pertaining to the month of Mādhava, just as it was seen and heard.”
Addressed thus by that sage, the hunter spoke with folded hands: / 15
“Not far from here there is water in a lake.
Kapittha trees are there, laden with a heavy load of fruit. / 16
Let us go there; contentment will be found, without a doubt.”
Directed thus by the hunter, the sage went along with him. / 17
Having gone some distance from there, he saw ahead a lake,
crowded with cranes and kāraṇḍavas, adorned with cakravākas, / 18
beautified all around by swans, sārasa cranes, and krauñcas,
resounding with loud resonant bamboos, and hummed over by bees, / 19
plunged into by crocodiles, turtles, fish, and the like, exceedingly enchanting,
vast with white water lilies, blue lotuses, kahlāras, and puṇḍarīkas, / 20
splendid all around with hundred-petaled lotuses and red water lilies,
resounding with the melodious calls of birds, a feast for the eyes, / 21
adorned on the bank with bamboo thickets and with trees:
with banyans, karañjas, nīpas, and ciñciṇīs, / 22
with nimba, plakṣa, priyāla, campaka, and auspicious bakula trees,
with punnāgas, tumburus, and also kapitthas and āmalakas, / 23
with niṣpeṣaṇa and jambū trees, adorned on every side;
with wild elephants, antelopes, boars, buffalos, and others, / 24
adorned with hares, porcupines, and forest oxen,
with rhinoceroses, musk deers, tigers, lions, and wolves, / 25
with donkeys, śarabhas, and beautifully adorned with deer;
with monkeys swiftly leaping from branch to branch, / 26
fearsome with wildcats, bears, and ruru deer,
with the sounds of crickets, shrieks, and the creaking of bamboos, / 27
endowed with masses of wood felled by violent windstorms—
such a divine lake was pointed out by the hunter. / 28
The tiger among sages, greatly tormented by thirst, saw it.
Having bathed at noon in this enchanting lake, / 29
putting on two garments, and then performing the midday rites,
he then performed worship of the gods and, alert, ate the fruit / 30
brought by the hunter—delicious kapittha fruit that removed his exhaustion.
Sitting comfortably, he asked the hunter who was devoted to righteousness: / 31
“What should I speak to you first today, O you who are dedicated to duty?
Duties are many, with diverse paths and different forms. / 32
Among them, those prescribed for the month of Vaiśākha, though subtle, yield great results;
they bestow rewards in this world and the next to all living beings. / 33
Whatever you need to ask in your mind, and whatever comes first, ask that.”
Addressed thus by that sage, he spoke with folded hands: / 34

2.7.m:
The hunter said:
"By what action did my birth as a hunter, full of darkness, arise?
By what [action] did such understanding or company with a great soul come about?
Tell me this and more, O Lord, if you think fit of me."
Thus addressed, the great sage named Śaṅkha spoke again,
with a voice deep as a thundercloud, his lotus-face gently smiling.
Śaṅkha said:
"Formerly, in the city of Śākala, you were a twice-born man, a master of the Vedas,
named Stamba, possessed of great splendor, born in the lineage of Śrīvatsa.
A certain courtesan became dear to you; and through the fault of association with her,
abandoning your daily rites, you returned home daily like a śūdra.
To you, devoid of conduct, wicked, and having cast off all religious duties,
there was at that time a wife, a brahmin woman named Kāntimatī.
That fair-browed woman served you, the lowest of brahmins, along with your courtesan.
Washing the feet of both, ever doing what pleased you,
she slept beneath both and was devoted to the words of both.
Though held back by the courtesan, she remained steadfast in her vow of wifely devotion.
As she thus attended upon her husband together with the courtesan,
a very long time passed for that sorrowful woman on the earth.
On another day, her husband ate black gram mixed with radishes,
[and] beans mixed with sesame—food customary for śūdras.
Having eaten that improper food, vomiting and purging,
from that unhealthy diet a terrible disease arose, fistula-in-ano.
He, tormented by that disease day and night exceedingly, [suffered].
As long as wealth remained in the house, so long did the courtesan stay.
Taking his wealth, she did not live in the house thereafter.
Approaching the side of another, that dreadful, pitiless woman departed.
Then, his speech pitiful, severely afflicted by the torment of disease,
he spoke, weeping, to his wife, his mind bewildered by pain:
'Protect me, O lady! I was attached to a courtesan, extremely cruel.

No kindness was done by me toward you, O beautiful, pure woman.
What vile sinner would not show respect to his devoted wife?
Such a one will become a eunuch, O auspicious woman, for fifteen births,
rebuked day and night by virtuous people, O blessed one!
I shall obtain a womb of sin, having truly disrespected you, a virtuous woman;
I am burned by the fire of anger born of dishonoring you.'
To her husband speaking thus, she said with folded hands:
'You should feel no dejection, nor shame toward me, O beloved!
Nor do I have anger toward you, by which you say you are burned now.
Sins committed in previous lives indeed turn into sorrows here.
That virtuous woman or that man who endures them is the best.
Whatever sin was committed by me, a sinner, in a previous birth,
as I experience that, I have no sorrow and no despair whatsoever.'

Knowing you to be averse to dharma, you were deceived under the pretext of a physician.

Embracing him with her arms, and clinging feet to feet,

and joining her hips to his hips, the noble lady, positioning herself,
caused the diseased body of her husband to be burned,
together with herself, that auspicious woman, in the blazing fire.
Abandoning her body, embracing her husband, she went instantly to the world of Murāri,
which is attainable by yogins, through the gift of water in this month of Mādhava and through the washing of [the sage's] feet.
You, having abandoned your body at the time of death while thinking of a courtesan, though freed of all evil,
obtained a birth as a hunter of terrible form, attached to violence, constantly causing terror.
Because assent was given by you to the gift of a cooling drink to a virtuous man in the month of Mādhava,
though born a hunter, there arose in you the noble intellect to ask about dharmas, the sole cause of all happiness.
The water left over from washing the sage's feet, which removes all sins, was placed on your head.

Because of that, you have this meeting with me in this forest, through which your prosperity and lineage will grow again.
Thus, all this has been told—whatever was done in your previous birth,
both meritorious action and sin, seen through divine vision.
I shall also tell you what is secret, whatever you wish to hear.
Purity of mind has indeed arisen in you; may there be welfare to you, O wise one!

2.7.m:
Dakṣa entered the genitals, [yet] that body did not rise up.
Indra then entered the hands, [yet] that body did not rise up.
The Sun entered the eye, [yet] that body did not rise up.
The quarters entered the ears, [yet] that body did not rise up.
Varuṇa entered the tongue, [yet] that body did not rise up.
The two Dasras entered the nose, [yet] that body did not rise up.
Fire entered the speech, [yet] that body did not rise up.
Rudra entered the mind, [yet] that body did not rise up.
Afterwards Prāṇa entered, and then the body rose up.
Then the gods, having determined that the all-pervading Prāṇa was superior to the gods
in strength, knowledge, courage, dispassion, and in vitalisation,
thereupon consecrated that great lord as the crown prince.
Because he was the cause of pre-eminent existence, they then sang a single praise:
"Therefore the universe, all that is mobile and immobile, consists of Prāṇa.
Rich in full and powerful portions, this [Prāṇa] is the lord of the worlds.
Nothing in the world is devoid of prāṇa; and devoid of prāṇa, nothing thrives.
Nothing exists here devoid of prāṇa, and nothing devoid of prāṇa exists.
Therefore Prāṇa became superior to all living beings, superior in strength, the inner self of all living beings."

2.7.m:
No one is seen in the scriptures, nor has ever been heard of, who is superior or even equal to Prāṇa.
Prāṇa attends to each and every function; indeed, he is one god acting in manifold ways.
Therefore, those dedicated to the worship of Prāṇa call Prāṇa supreme.
He is capable of creating, destroying, and maintaining the world merely in play.
Even the sentient and the insentient, beginning with Śeṣa the serpent, Śiva, and Indra—
none except Vāsudeva can ever surpass him.
Prāṇa consists of all gods; the all-pervading one is made up of all gods.
He constantly follows Vāsudeva and abides under Viṣṇu's command.
He neither hears nor sees anything opposed to Vāsudeva.
The gods, beginning with Rudra and the lords of the celestials, act in opposition,
but Prāṇa, whose range is everywhere, never acts in opposition anywhere.
Therefore the wise call Prāṇa the power of Mahāviṣṇu.
Knowing thus the greatness and nature of Mahāviṣṇu,
casting off the subtle body bound to previous ties as a snake casts off worn-out skin,
one goes to the supreme, taintless Nārāyaṇa."
Having heard the words spoken by Śaṅkha, the hunter, joyful in mind,
bowed low in reverence and questioned that sage again:
"O brāhmaṇa, why is the glory of this noble Prāṇa, the guru of the world,
the sovereign lord of all, not proclaimed in the world?
The glory of gods, sages, and noble kings
is heard by the thousands in the world within the Purāṇas.
Tell me this, O brāhmaṇa, for I have a great curiosity to hear it."
Śaṅkha said:
"Long ago, Prāṇa, desiring to sacrifice to the god Hari, the taintless Nārāyaṇa,
with horse-sacrifices, went joyfully to the bank of the Gaṅgā.
Accompanied by various hosts of sages, he prepared the ground with plows.
Inside an ant-hill lay absorbed in meditation one named Kaṇva.

2.7.m:
Uprooted by the plow, he came out and spoke in anger.
Seeing Prāṇa standing before him, he cursed the great, all-pervading lord:
'From this day forward, O lord of gods, your greatness shall not attain fame
in the three worlds, and particularly upon the earth.
Your incarnations, however, will be celebrated throughout the three worlds.'
Thus addressed by that sage, Vāyu angrily said to him:

2.7.m:
'Without fault, forgiving and guiltless though I am, I have been cursed.
Therefore, O mighty-armed Kaṇva, quickly become a betrayer of your guru,
and may your livelihood be despised in the world!' so spoke the Ever-Moving One.
From that time forward, O great lord, the greatness of this Prāṇa
has not been celebrated in this world, especially upon the earth.
Due to the curse, Kaṇva consumed his guru and then became a disciple of Sūrya.
Thus all of this, which you have just asked, has been related.
Whatever else you have to hear, O hunter, ask me without hesitation."
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, named 'The Account of the Curse of Vāyu', in the dialogue between Nārada and Ambarīṣa, in the Vaiśākhamāsamāhātmya, in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

2.7.m: The hunter said: / Auspicious Bhāgavata duties directed toward Viṣṇu should be performed, / and especially those pertaining to the month of Mādhava—so it was said by you before. / What is that Viṣṇu like, O brahmin? Or what indeed is his defining characteristic? / What is the proof of his true being? By what means is the lordly Bhagavān to be known? / What are the Vaiṣṇava duties like? By what is that Hari pleased? / Tell me this, O wise brahmin, to me, your servant! / Questioned thus by the hunter, the twice-born said again, / having bowed to Nārāyaṇa, the lord of the worlds, free from affliction: / Śaṅkha said: / Listen, O hunter! I will tell you the stainless form of Viṣṇu, / which is unthinkable [even] by Brahmā and the other sages of cultivated mind. / Possessing full power, possessing full qualities, he is designated the Lord of all; / devoid of [material] qualities, undivided, infinite, his form is being, consciousness, and bliss. / This entire universe, moving and unmoving, incomparable, / which rests on him as supreme support, remains continuously under his control. / Now I shall tell you the defining characteristic of Brahman, the Supreme Self: / From whom arise creation, maintenance, destruction, cycle [of rebirth], regulation, / illumination, bondage and liberation, and livelihood— / that Viṣṇu is called Brahman; he is considered all-pervading by the wise. / They call him directly Brahman, and afterward even Brahmā and the others; / the wise know the word 'brahman' applied to Brahmā and others as accompanied by an epithet. / In no other beings does Brahmanhood exist, for they possess only a single fraction of his power. / This [nature] of his, the great all-pervading Lord, originating [the universe] and so forth, is accessible only through scripture. / And scripture consists of the Vedas, the Smṛtis, the Purāṇa identical in nature to them, / the Itihāsa, the Pañcarātra, and the Bhārata, O wise one! / Only through these can Mahāviṣṇu be known, by no other means whatsoever; / a man who does not know the Vedas never comprehends this Viṣṇu. / Not by the senses, nor by inferences, nor by arguments can the all-pervading Lord, / the god Nārāyaṇa, knowable through the Vedas, eternal, be known. / Having known according to one's capacity his births, deeds, and qualities alone,

2.7.m: the multitudes of living beings, who are always subject to his control, are liberated. / In order that the greatness of Viṣṇu may become pre-eminent, / a power resides in each one among the gods, sages, ancestors, and mother goddesses. / Through direct perception, through scripture, and likewise through inference, / one should first know the best of men in strength, knowledge, and happiness. / Greater by a hundredfold than him one should know a spirit endowed with knowledge and the like; / one should know the human Gandharvas to be a hundred times greater than spirits. / The gods who identify with the elements should be known as a hundred times greater than them; / superior to the gods who identify with the elements are the seven seers alone. / Superior indeed to the seven seers is Agni; from Agni, Sūrya and the others; / from Sūrya, Bṛhaspati; from Bṛhaspati, Prāṇa; from Prāṇa, Indra of great strength; / and superior to Indra is the goddess Girijā; superior to the goddess is Śambhu, the guru of the universe; / superior to Śambhu is Buddhi, the great goddess; superior to Buddhi is Prāṇa, greater in strength. / There is nothing higher than Prāṇa; everything is established in Prāṇa; / from Prāṇa this universe was born; this world is composed of Prāṇa; / everything here is woven upon Prāṇa; indeed, it moves only because of Prāṇa. / They call him the support of all, the Sūtra, having the luster of a dark blue cloud. / By a mere glance of Lakṣmī alone can this Prāṇa maintain his state; / that Lakṣmī possesses only a small fraction of the grace of the God of gods. / There is nothing higher than Viṣṇu, nor is there anyone equal to him in any way. / The hunter said: / How did this Prāṇa, named Sūtra, become superior among living beings? / Or how is this established? How is the superiority of Prāṇa [explained], O lord? / Tell me this, O brahmin: how is the Lord superior to Prāṇa? / Śaṅkha said: / Listen, O hunter! I will tell you the determination as asked, / regarding the superiority of Prāṇa over all living beings as well. / Formerly, the eternal god Nārāyaṇa, during the lotus creation, / having created Brahmā and the other gods, Janārdana said this: / 'I shall place Brahmā in supreme sovereignty as your master and lord, / and whoever is the superior god among you, O lords of the gods, in the position of heir-apparent.

2.7.m:
"Install him who is rich in good conduct, endowed with the qualities of valour and generosity."
Having been thus spoken to by the Lord, all the gods, led by Indra,
disputed among one another in this way, saying, "I should be [he]," and "I [should be he]!"
And as they all disputed, some considered the Sun to be supreme;
some considered Indra supreme, others Kāma, while yet others stood silent.
Seeing no resolution, they went to Nārāyaṇa to ask.
Having bowed down, all the immortals said again with folded hands:
"This was deliberated truly by all of us, O Mahāviṣṇu,
[yet] we do not know at all who is the superior god among us.
You alone tell us the decision; for the gods are indeed full of doubt."
Thus questioned by all the immortals, he smiled and said this:
"He upon whose departure from this cosmic body it indeed
falls, and upon whose entrance it surely rises up,
that god is indeed superior; definitely none other at all."
Being thus addressed, all of them then said, "So be it."
First, the ruler of gods named Jayanta departed from the foot.
Then they called this [body] lame, but the body did not fall then:
hearing, drinking, speaking, smelling, seeing, it remained, even without moving.
Afterwards, the lord of creatures named Dakṣa departed from the genitals.
Then they called this [body] a eunuch, but the body did not fall then:
hearing, drinking, speaking, smelling, seeing, it remained, even moving.
Afterwards, Indra, the lord of all immortals, departed from the hands.
They called this [body] handless, but the body did not fall then:
hearing, drinking, speaking, smelling, seeing, it remained, even moving.
From the eyes departed the Sun, the best of the luminous.
Then they called this [body] blind in one eye, but the body did not fall then:
hearing, drinking, speaking, smelling, seeing, it remained, even moving.
Afterwards, from the nose departed the two Nāsatyas, the universal physicians.
They called this [body] devoid of smell, but the body did not fall then:

hearing, drinking, speaking, not smelling at all, it remained, even without moving.
From the ear the quarters departed, but the body did not fall then;
they then called this [body] deaf, but by no means dead:
drinking, speaking, even then not hearing, yet without moving.
Varuṇa then departed from the tongue after that;
then they called it merely devoid of taste, but the body did not fall then:
living, moving, eating, it remained, and likewise knowing and breathing.
Then from speech departed Fire, the lord of speech, the all-pervading.
Then they called this [body] mute, but the body did not fall then:
living, moving, eating, it remained, and likewise knowing and breathing.
Afterwards Rudra departed from the mind, the essence of consciousness.
Then they called this [body] inert, but the body did not fall then:
living, moving, eating, it remained, and likewise knowing and breathing.
Afterwards Prāṇa departed; then they knew this [body] to be dead.
Then, with astonished minds, the gods spoke again thus:
"He who can raise the body that has come to this state,
he alone will indeed be the superior among us, and will become the crown prince."
Having thus agreed, they entered [it] in proper order:
Jayanta entered the feet, [yet] that body did not rise up.

2.7.m:
The story of Vālmīki's previous birth.
The hunter said:
"Were living beings created by the omnipresent Lord by the millions and thousands?
Eternal, they are seen to have diverse actions and various paths. / 1
Whence do these [beings] have not a single nature, O highly intelligent one?
To me who ask all this, speak in full according to the truth." / 2
Śaṅkha said:
"Living beings are threefold indeed, possessing the qualities of rajas, sattva, and tamas.
Rājasic beings perform rājasic actions; likewise, tāmasic beings perform tāmasic actions. / 3
Sāttvic beings perform sāttvic actions, each in due order.
And sometimes, an inequality of qualities arises for them in the cycle of worldly existence. / 4
Performing high and low actions by that very reason, they share in their fruits:
sometimes happiness, sometimes misery, and sometimes both together. / 5
These men attain [such states] solely through the inequality of the qualities.
Abiding in material nature, these living beings are bound by these three qualities. / 6
According to quality and action, there is a variation of fruits for actions.
By the conformity to their qualities, these people repeatedly return to material nature. / 7
Abiding in material nature, bound to material nature, bewildered by qualities and actions,
they go to the material destiny; indeed, there is no departure from material nature. / 8
Tāmasic beings are full of misery, ever having tāmasic conduct,
pitiless, harsh in the world, ever living solely on malice. / 9
Beginning with the rākṣasas and ending with the piśācas, they certainly attain a tāmasic destiny.
Rājasic beings have mixed minds, performers of merit and sin. / 10
Through merit they attain heaven, and sometimes through sin, torment.
Therefore, these unfortunate ones revolve again and again. / 11
Righteous in conduct, compassionate, full of faith, free from envy,
sāttvic beings remain practicing sāttvic conduct. / 12
And they, spotless and possessed of great splendor, go upward when the qualities depart.
And therefore, beings of diverse actions have diverse states of various kinds. / 13
According to their qualities and actions, Lord Viṣṇu, the supreme master,
truly impels them to deeds, the omnipresent one, so they may attain their true nature. / 14
Partiality and cruelty do not belong to Viṣṇu, whose desires are fully fulfilled;
he carries out creation, preservation, and destruction with complete impartiality. / 15
Solely through their own qualities do all of them partake in the fruit of action,
just as [rain] falls equally on all the trees planted in a garden. / 16
Watered by a single channel, dear one, the trees follow their own nature;
there is no partiality or cruelty whatever in the planter of the garden." / 17
The hunter said:
"When can there be liberation for people who have fully experienced their fruits, O sage?
Is it at the time of creation, or at the time of end, or of maintenance? / 18
And also, Brahman, explain to me in detail the time of creation, dissolution, and maintenance—
speak of this activity of the Lord." / 19
Śaṅkha said:
"A thousand sets of four yugas is said to be a day of Brahmā,
and his night is of equal length; a day and night constitutes [one full] day. / 20
Fifteen days they call a fortnight; a month consists of two [fortnights].
Two months they call a season, and three seasons an ayana. / 21
Two ayanas make a year. If a hundred such years
pass for this Brahmā, they know that as a brahmakalpa. / 22
The period of dissolution is of equal length: such is the view of knowers of the Veda.
Dissolution is declared to be threefold: human, at the end of a Manu's period; / 23
the second is daily, at the end of Brahmā's day;
and after the dissolution of Brahmā, they know it as the brāhma dissolution." / 24
