2.7.m: In a muhūrta of Brahmā, however, they know of the dissolution of a Manu. / When fourteen dissolutions have passed in succession, / they speak of the daily dissolution, and again of the duration of the dissolutions. / The dissolution of the three worlds takes place in a manvantara; / then there is destruction of conscious beings, but not a destruction of the worlds. / And there is filling up with waters, just as before, so again / at the end of a manvantara there is the rebirth of conscious beings. / In the daily dissolution, O hunter, there is destruction of everything. / Except for Satyaloka, all worlds perish along with their regents, / along with sentient beings and elemental spirits, when the four-faced one has fallen asleep. / The gods presiding over the principles and some sages likewise, / situated in Satyaloka, remain asleep, all of them. / Having entered sleep, beyond the senses, they remain for as long as a kalpa. / Again, at the end of night, Brahmā fashioned as before / the seers, the gods, the ancestors, the worlds, the duties, and the classes separately. / Again, the ten incarnations of the lord Viṣṇu, holder of the discus, / these occur by fixed rule, and likewise many others. / And the deities and seers, unto the end of the kalpa of the lord of speech, / turn back again, attaining liberation together with Brahmā. / And the virtuous kings who attained perfection and achieved the supreme, / turn back likewise, dwelling in Satyaloka. / Those belonging to that collection go again under that name, established in the Vedas. / They are born in those respective lineages, always devoted to those respective actions. / For all the Daityas too, when the end of the Kali age arrives, / they go to their own state, dwelling in hell, together with Kali. / And those belonging to their collection, and others bearing their names, / are born according to their own karma, performative of those respective acts. / I shall declare the time of creation and likewise the time of liberation / of Brahmā and the other gods; become concentrated in mind. / The closing of the eyes of the god of gods is considered equal to a kalpa of Brahmā; / at the end of that is the opening of the eyes of the crest-jewel among the gods of gods. / At the end of the closing of the eyes, there is the wish to create the worlds resting in his belly. / In his own belly he saw all the multitude of beings manifoldly, / those to be created and those liberated, who have attained the dissolution of the subtle body, / all asleep, those situated in the cycle of birth, and also those in darkness in every way. / In the previous kalpa, those from Brahmā downwards who attained dissolution of the subtle body, / reaching down to humans, the sheaths of living beings, both living-liberated and destined for liberation, / and those liberated in a previous kalpa, from Brahmā down to humans, / remain established in meditation, even while inside Viṣṇu's belly. / In the first part of the eye-opening, the all-pervading lord, having assumed the form of the four emanations, / by his primordial excellence and from Vāsudeva who is part of the emanation, / having bestowed upon Brahmā liberation named sāyujya, the great all-pervading lord, / having then given sāyujya and knowledge of reality to the noble-minded ones, / and sārūpya to some, and sāmīpya likewise, the all-pervading lord, / and having given sālokya to others, the divine Janārdana / looked upon all the worlds situated under the control of Aniruddha. / Giving [creation] over to the control of Pradyumna, he set his mind to create; / Hari himself wedded Māyā, Jayā, Kṛti, and Śānti.

2.7.m:
Through the four emanations, Vāsudeva and the rest, possessing complete qualities in succession, / united with them, the great Viṣṇu, the all-pervading lord composed of the four emanations, / his desires fulfilled, brought forth the world with its diverse receptacles of action. / At the end of the eye-opening, Viṣṇu, resorting again to Yogamāyā, / through Saṃkarṣaṇa belonging to the emanation, withdraws this universe of moving and unmoving beings. / All this has been declared: the work of the Great Soul to be meditated upon, / which is unthinkable and difficult to comprehend even by yogins such as Brahmā.
The hunter said: / What are the duties of the Bhāgavatas, by which Viṣṇu is pleased? / I wish to hear them now; speak to us, O sage.
Śaṅkha said: / That by which there is purity of mind, which is beneficial to the good, / know that to be sattvic duty, and that which is blameless by anyone. / That which is enjoined by Śruti and Smṛti, if it is free from desire, / and that which is not opposed to the world, they know that to be sattvic duty. / For these duties are fourfold according to the division of classes and stages of life. / Regular, occasional, and optional: thus they are considered threefold. / When all those duties of one's own are surrendered to Viṣṇu, / then indeed they should be known as sattvic, auspicious Bhāgavata duties. / Duties having other deities as their divinity, accompanied by desire, are considered rajasic. / Having yakṣas, rakṣasas, piśācas, and the like as deities, cruel to the world, / consisting of violence and censured: those duties are recorded as tamasic. / Situated in sattva, people perform sattvic duties, pleasing to Viṣṇu and auspicious, / constantly without selfish longing; they indeed are recorded as Bhāgavatas.

Having bathed at sunrise in the morning, listening to what is recited by the foremost brahmin, (77)

With an attentive mind, one should listen to the narrative concerning the month of Mādhava. (78)
One should avoid oil-massage and eating from a bronze vessel;
one should avoid forbidden foods, and idle conversation. (79)

Indian spinach, *kaliṅga*, and drumstick leaves—these one must avoid;
flat beans, horse gram, and lentils one must also avoid. (81)
Eggplants, watermelons, and kodo millet one must avoid;
*taṇḍulīyaka* greens, safflower, and radish; (82)
cluster-fig fruit, bael fruit, and the fruit of the *śleṣmātaka* tree—
a wise person should strictly avoid all these in this month dear to Mādhava. (83)
Eating any one of these, he certainly becomes an outcaste;
he passes through a hundred animal wombs; on this there is no doubt. (84)
Thus one should observe the monthly vow for the pleasure of the slayer of Madhu.
And when the vow is thus concluded, one should have an image of the Lord made, (85)
dedicated to Madhusūdana, accompanied by garments and an offering of fees,
and, having worshipped it well with all resources, present it to a brahmin. (86)
On the bright twelfth day of Vaiśākha, one should duly offer curd-rice,
along with a water jar, betel, fruit, and a sacrificial fee: (87)
“I give [this] to Dharmarāja; through this may Yama be pleased.”

Then, having recited from the sacred thread over the right shoulder the name and lineage of one's father, (88)
one should give imperishable curd-rice for the satisfaction of the ancestors;
likewise one should give to teachers, and afterwards to Viṣṇu: (89)
“This excellent curd-rice with cold water, kept in a bronze vessel,
together with a fee, betel, food-offerings, and fruit, (90)
I give to you, Viṣṇu, out of a desire to attain Viṣṇu's world.”
Having given thus according to one's capacity, one should also give a cow to a householder. (91)
Whoever performs the monthly vow in this manner, free from deceit,
is freed from all sins, and, having delivered a hundred ancestors of his lineage, (92)
piercing the solar disc before the very eyes of all living beings,
he goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu, difficult of access even for yogins. (93)
While the best of brahmins was thus explaining the duties belonging to Mādhava,
the exceedingly beneficial duties pleasing to Viṣṇu and others, inquired about by the hunter, (94)
that banyan tree, a five-branched tree, suddenly fell to the earth before their very eyes, oh wonder!

2.7.m:
"The story of Vālmīki's previous birth.
Śrutadeva said:
'Then Śaṅkha, accompanied by the hunter, became astonished
and said to him: "Who are you, and whence comes this condition of yours? 1
Or by what deed, gentle one, has your mind become bearer of good fortune?
How did your liberation come about suddenly? Tell this in detail." 2
Being then asked thus by Śaṅkha, falling like a stick upon the earth,
bowed in modesty, he spoke this word with joined palms: 3
"Formerly I was a certain talkative twice-born in Prayāga,
endowed with beauty and youth, very arrogant with the pride of learning, 4
rich in wealth, rich in many sons, constantly corrupted by egotism,
the son of the sage Kusīda, Rocana by name. 5
Sitting, lying down, sleeping, intercourse, playing dice,
gossip of the world, or usury—those were my occupations. 6
Fearing the censure of people, I always performed only superficial actions
with hypocrisy, and never had any faith. 7
Some time passed for me, wicked and of corrupt intellect.
Then, in this month of Vaiśākha, a certain twice-born named Jayanta 8
caused the virtues of that month, dear to the devotees of the Lord,
to be heard by the twice-born residents of that holy field, performers of meritorious deeds. 9
Women, men, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras in the thousands,
having bathed in the morning and fully worshipped the imperishable Madhusūdana..." 2.7.21.10

and having betel in my mouth, I wore a tunic. (13)
I caused distraction from the narration by amusing [them] with idle worldly talk;
there arose agitation in the minds of everyone on account of that gossip. (14)
Stretching out my garment in one place, censuring someone in another, laughing elsewhere,
in this manner time was spent by me until the story came to an end. (15)

2.7.m:
Afterwards, by that very fault, my intellect ruined and short-lived, / I met death from high fever on the very next day.
Reaching the hell named Halāhala, filled with waters of molten lead, / and suffering torment for fourteen Manvantaras,
and then in eighty-four lakhs / of wombs in succession, I was born; and now I was dwelling in a tree
ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas high, / a cruel, dark serpent in a hollow of seven yojanas.
Having become that, I have lived there, O brahmin seer, afflicted by former karma; / ten thousand years have passed as I remained fasting in the tree-hollow.
By fortune, having heard with both eyes from the lotus of your mouth the nectar of the narrative, / my misfortune was instantly destroyed, O sage.
Casting off the serpent-birth, I have become a man bearing a divine form; / folding my hands in reverence and bowing, I have taken refuge at your feet.
I do not know in which lifetime you were my relative, O best of sages. / I never rendered you any service; whence this compassion of the virtuous?
The nature of virtuous people, whose minds are impartial and who always have pity for living beings, / is doing good to others, and their thought is never otherwise.
Bless me today so that my mind may dwell on righteousness, / and that forgetfulness of Lord Viṣṇu, the wielder of the discus, may never occur anywhere.
May there always be fellowship with the great who act virtuously! / Poverty alone can be the supreme collyrium for one blinded by pride.'
Having praised him in many ways thus, and bowing again and again, / he stood quietly before him with folded hands, bowing down.
Śaṅkha, raising him with his arms, overflowing with complete love, / touched his body with his hand, most auspicious and dispelling weariness.
He bestowed grace on that brahmin who possessed a divine form, / and filled with compassion, he directly told him the future events:
'O brahmin, from hearing the māhātmya of the month and from hearing the māhātmya / of Hari, all your bonds have been instantly shattered.
Having cast off your stain and going again to the earth in due course, / you will become an excellent brahmin in the uneven, sacred Daśārṇa country.

2.7.m:
Renowned by the name Vedaśarman, expert in all the Vedas, / you will have the continuous, auspicious memory of your past births there.
Thus bound to remembrance, having abandoned all desires, auspicious, / you will perform all the religious duties enjoined in Vaiśākha, dear to Hari.
Free from dualities, without longing, unattached, devoted to the guru, having conquered the senses, / always conversing on the narratives of Viṣṇu, you will be in that birth.
Then, having attained perfection and all bonds being shattered, / you will reach the supreme abode, difficult to attain even through yogas.
Do not fear, my son; good fortune will be yours through my grace. / Out of jest, out of fear, likewise out of anger, malice, or even desire,
or out of affection, having uttered once the name of Viṣṇu which removes sins, / even the most sinful go to the disease-free abode of Viṣṇu.
How much more then, O best of brahmins, do they go who, endowed with faith, / with anger subdued and senses mastered, and full of compassion, hear the sacred narrative!
Some, through devotion alone, intent solely on the discourse of his stories, / though devoid of all other duties, go to the supreme foot of Viṣṇu.
Some worship Viṣṇu through hatred and the like, or through devotion; / they too go to the supreme abode, just like Pūtanā who took away his life.
Constant association with the great and speech dedicated to taking refuge in him / must be maintained by those desiring liberation; this is the rule enjoined by the scriptures.
That utterance of words destroys the sins of the people, in which, though each verse may be poorly composed, / the names of the Infinite One, marked by his glory, are heard, sung, and recited by the virtuous.
Which compassionate one would one take refuge in, other than the all-pervading Lord, who desires neither strenuous service, / nor immense wealth, nor beauty and youth, but when remembered even once, leads to the radiant abode?
Go to him alone for refuge, the unblemished Nārāyaṇa, / who is affectionate to his devotees, unmanifest, accessible to the intellect, an ocean of compassion.
Perform all these religious duties declared in Vaiśākha, O highly intelligent one; / pleased thereby, the Lord of the Universe will bestow happiness upon you.'
Having spoken thus, he fell silent, and seeing the hunter, he was greatly amazed; / that divine person again spoke to that foremost of sages:

2.7.m:
The divine person said:
"I am blessed, I am favored by you, O compassionate Śaṅkha!
Fortunately, my wretched birth has ended, and I go indeed to the supreme destination." 47.
Having thus circumambulated him and received permission, he went to heaven.
Then it became evening, O King; Śaṅkha, pleased by the hunter,
performed the evening twilight prayers and passed the rest of the night
with various stories of kings and noble deities,
with the pastimes of the incarnations, and with visible assemblies.
Arising at the hour sacred to Brahmā, washing his feet, restraining his speech, / meditating on the saving Brahman, and performing purification and proper rites,
having bathed in Vaiśākha while the sun was in Aries and before the rising of the stars,
performing the twilight rituals and other rites, and satisfying all [the gods and ancestors],
he called the hunter, joyful in mind, sprinkled [water] on his head, looked at him,
and gave the two-syllabled, auspicious name 'Rāma', which is superior to the Vedas.
Even each single name of Viṣṇu is considered superior to all the Vedas;
and superior to those infinite names is the thousand names.

2.7.m:
The name of Rāma is considered equal to such a thousand names.
"Therefore, O hunter, mutter that name 'Rāma' continuously;
perform these duties, O hunter, until the end of your life.
Then your birth will take place in the family of the seer Valmīka,
and you will attain fame on earth by the name Vālmīki."
Having thus instructed the hunter, he set out towards the southern direction.
The hunter too, having circumambulated him and bowed again and again,
followed him for some distance, weeping and afflicted by separation.
As far as the path of sight extended, he watched his departure again,
and returned with difficulty, contemplating him alone in his heart.
Constructing a forest dwelling and making a pure water booth on that path,
He performed indeed these most fitting duties prescribed for the month of Vaiśākha,
with wild wood-apples, jackfruits, rose-apples, mangoes, and other fruits,
providing food for those suffering fatigue on the road;
and with sandals, sandalwood, umbrellas, and even fans,
and here and there with shades provided with layers of sand,

2.7.m:
he dispelled the weariness and sweat born of exertion in travelers.
Bathing at dawn and murmuring day and night the mantra, 'Rāma',
in his hunter's birth he became known as the son of Valmīka.
A certain sage named Kṛṇu, at that very lake,
practiced indeed severe austerity, devoid of external activity.
In course of long time, an anthill (valmīka) formed over his body;
therefore they called that foremost among sages 'Valmīka'.
Afterward, at the conclusion of the cessation of austerities, when Kṛṇu returned to ordinary consciousness,
as he remembered a woman, O king, semen fell from the sage.
A certain actress received it; in her was born that forest-dweller
renowned throughout the worlds as Vālmīki, of great renown,
who made known to the world the divine story of Rāma through his charming compositions,
which cuts through the bonds of karma.
Śrutadeva said:
Behold the greatness of Vaiśākha, O king, which yields prosperity even to this day!
Even a hunter, by giving a pair of sandals, attained the hard-to-attain status of a seer.

2.7.m:
Whoever hears or recites this supreme narrative,
which destroys sins and causes the hair to bristle with joy, shall never again suck a mother's breast.

2.7.m:
The son of Mithilā said:
Which lunar days are holy in this month named Vaiśākha? / Which gifts are praised specifically on which of those days?
Which are famous in the world? Tell me this in detail.
Śrutadeva said:
All thirty lunar days are holy in Vaiśākha when the sun is in Aries.
Merit acquired on an Ekādaśī becomes multiplied a hundred millionfold. / Whatever merit there is in all gifts, whatever fruit in all sacred fords,
one attains it entirely when bathed in water on an Ekādaśī in Vaiśākha. / Bathing, gift-giving, austerity, oblation, pious acts of worshiping deities,
and listening to the narrative bring about immediate liberation. / Even one afflicted by diseases and the like, or oppressed by poverty,
becomes fulfilled upon hearing this holy narrative. / One by whom these auspicious [days] are spent without bathing and without giving,
is considered a slayer of cows, an ungrateful person, and a great slayer of his ancestors. / Reservoirs of water are accessible, and one's body is under one's control;
Mādhava is to be served with the mind, and the season is endowed with the best of virtues. / The virtuous are compassionate—who would not serve Mādhava?
By the poor, by the rich, by the lame, and by the blind, / by eunuchs, by widows, by women, and likewise by men,
by children, youth, and the elderly, and even by the sick, O protector of the earth: / the religious duty within the sphere of Vaiśākha is indeed extremely easy to perform.
Having reached this month, perform these auspicious duties. / Who does not make an effort? What other [month] could be more auspicious than this?
The lowest of men who does not perform these extremely accessible duties, / for him alone hellish worlds are easily attained; of this there is no doubt.
Now, therefore, I shall declare what is the best lunar day in that month, / that day which destroys all sins, extracted like the essence of curd.
In the exceedingly holy month of Caitra, when the sun is stationed in Aries, / destroying sins, having the ancestors as its deities, granting the fruit of ten million Gayās;
right here a holy ancient song about the ancestors is heard. / Listen, O king, to that true story: while Sāvarṇi was ruling the earth,
at the end of thirty Kaliyugas, when all religious duty was abandoned, / in Ānarta there was a certain twice-born known as Dharmavarṇa.
Seeing people engaged in sin in the Kaliyuga, O king, / in its very first quarter, bereft of the duties of caste;
he once went to the sacrificial session of the great-souled sages, / who were observing silence, in the sacred field of Puṣkara.
There, holy discourses of the seers pertaining to the scriptures were held; / there, certain ones steadfast in their vows praised the Kaliyuga:
'The merit pleasing Mādhava which in the Kṛtayuga takes a year to achieve, / in the Tretā takes a month, and in the Dvāpara a fortnight, O king;
therefore, from remembering Viṣṇu in the Kaliyuga, the merit is tenfold. / Even very little merit becomes ten millionfold in the Kaliyuga.
When [the world] is devoid of compassion and merit, and destitute of charity and duty, / if one exercises compassion and gives a gift, uttering the name of Hari even once,
he surely goes upward; and likewise one who gives food in a famine.' / On the occasion of this discourse, the sage Nārada arrived,
holding his penis with one hand and his tongue with the other, laughing, / and like a madman, that best of sages danced there.
The assembly members then asked him: 'What is this, O Nārada?' / That wise one, still dancing and laughing, replied to them all:

2.7.s:
saṃtoṣādyadiha proktaṃ nṛtyadbhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ ..
siddhā vayaṃ na saṃdehaḥ puṇyo'yaṃ kalirāgataḥ .. 26 ..
tatsatyaṃ na ca saṃdeho bahu svalpena sādhyate ..
smaraṇāttoṣamāyāti keśavaḥ kleśanāśanaḥ .. 27 ..
tathāpi vaḥ pravakṣyāmi durghaṭaṃ ca dvayaṃ dhuvam ..
śiśnasya nigrahaḥ putrā jihvāyā api nityaśaḥ .. 28 ..
dvayaṃ yaddhi bhavedyasya sa eva syājjanārdanaḥ ..
bhavadbhirnātra sthātavyaṃ tasmātkaliyugāgame .. 29 ..
pākhaṃḍaṃ bhārataṃ hitvā saṃcaradhvaṃ yathāsukham ..
yatra kutrāpi deśeṣu mano yatra prasīdati .. 2.7.22.30 ..
iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ ..
satraṃ samāpya sahasā yayuste ca yathāsukham .. 31 ..
dharmavarṇo'pi tacchrutvā tyaktuṃ bhūmiṃ mano dadhe ..
sa vrataṃ cordhvatejaskaṃ dhṛtvā daṇḍakamaḍalū .. 32 ..
jaṭāvalkaladhārī ca bhūtvā caivaṃ yayau punaḥ ..
2.7.d:
संतोषाद्यदिह प्रोक्तं नृत्यद्भिर्भावितात्मभिः ..
सिद्धा वयं न संदेहः पुण्योऽयं कलिरागतः .. 26 ..
तत्सत्यं न च संदेहो बहु स्वल्पेन साध्यते ..
स्मरणात्तोषमायाति केशवः क्लेशनाशनः .. 27 ..
तथापि वः प्रवक्ष्यामि दुर्घटं च द्वयं धुवम् ..
शिश्नस्य निग्रहः पुत्रा जिह्वाया अपि नित्यशः .. 28 ..
द्वयं यद्धि भवेद्यस्य स एव स्याज्जनार्दनः ..
भवद्भिर्नात्र स्थातव्यं तस्मात्कलियुगागमे .. 29 ..
पाखंडं भारतं हित्वा संचरध्वं यथासुखम् ..
यत्र कुत्रापि देशेषु मनो यत्र प्रसीदति .. 2.7.22.30 ..
इति तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा मुनयः शंसितव्रताः ..
सत्रं समाप्य सहसा ययुस्ते च यथासुखम् .. 31 ..
धर्मवर्णोऽपि तच्छ्रुत्वा त्यक्तुं भूमिं मनो दधे ..
स व्रतं चोर्ध्वतेजस्कं धृत्वा दण्डकमडलू .. 32 ..
जटावल्कलधारी च भूत्वा चैवं ययौ पुनः ..
2.7.m:
'What has been said here out of delight by you dancing ones whose minds are purified,
that "we have achieved our aim, there is no doubt, this holy Kali has arrived"—
that is true, without doubt; much is achieved through very little;
Keśava, the destroyer of distress, becomes pleased through mere remembrance.
Nevertheless, I shall tell you of two things that are certainly difficult to accomplish:
the control of the penis, O sons, and of the tongue constantly.
He who possesses both of these would indeed be Janārdana himself.
Therefore, you must not stay here upon the arrival of the Kaliyuga.
Leave this heretical Bhārata and wander about at your ease,
anywhere in whatever lands your mind finds peace.'
Having heard those words of his, the sages celebrated for their vows...
Completing the sacrificial session, they quickly went away at their ease.
Hearing that, Dharmavarṇa also resolved in his mind to leave the earth.
Assuming an ascetic observance of lofty splendour, taking a staff and water pot,
wearing matted hair and bark garments, he departed once again,

2.7.s:
kalau yuge tvanācārāndraṣṭuṃ vismitamānasaḥ .. 33 ..
tatrā'paśyajjanānghorānpāpācāraratānkhalān ..

bhartāraṃ dveṣṭi bhāryā ca śiṣyo dveṣṭi guruṃ tathā ..
bhṛtyaśca svāmihaṃtā ca putraḥ pitṛvadhe rataḥ .. 35 ..
śūdraprāyā dvijāḥ sarve bastaprāyāśca dhenavaḥ ..
gāthāprāyāstathā vedāḥ kriyāsāmyāḥ śubhāḥ kriyāḥ .. 36 ..
bhūtapretapiśācādyāḥ phaladāstatra devatāḥ ..
tā eva śraddhayā'rcaṃti janāḥ pāparatāḥ śitāḥ .. 37 ..
sarve vyavāyaniratāstadarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ ..

manasyekaṃ vacasyekaṃ karmaṇyekaṃ sadā kalau ..
sarveṣāṃ haitukī vidyā sā pūjyā nṛpamaṃdire .. 39 ..
gītādyāśca kalā vidyā nṛpāṇāṃ ca priyāvahāḥ ..
hīnāśca pūjyatāṃ yāṃti nottamāśca kalau yuge .. 2.7.22.40 ..
2.7.d:
कलौ युगे त्वनाचारान्द्रष्टुं विस्मितमानसः .. 33 ..
तत्राऽपश्यज्जनान्घोरान्पापाचाररतान्खलान् ..
पाखण्डिनो द्विजाः सर्वे शूद्राः प्रव्राजिनस्तथा .. 34 ..
भर्तारं द्वेष्टि भार्या च शिष्यो द्वेष्टि गुरुं तथा ..
भृत्यश्च स्वामिहंता च पुत्रः पितृवधे रतः .. 35 ..
शूद्रप्राया द्विजाः सर्वे बस्तप्रायाश्च धेनवः ..
गाथाप्रायास्तथा वेदाः क्रियासाम्याः शुभाः क्रियाः .. 36 ..
भूतप्रेतपिशाचाद्याः फलदास्तत्र देवताः ..
ता एव श्रद्धयाऽर्चंति जनाः पापरताः शिताः .. 37 ..
सर्वे व्यवायनिरतास्तदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ..
कूटसाक्ष्यप्रवक्तारः सदा कैतवमानसाः .. 38 ..
मनस्येकं वचस्येकं कर्मण्येकं सदा कलौ ..
सर्वेषां हैतुकी विद्या सा पूज्या नृपमंदिरे .. 39 ..
गीताद्याश्च कला विद्या नृपाणां च प्रियावहाः ..
हीनाश्च पूज्यतां यांति नोत्तमाश्च कलौ युगे .. 2.7.22.40 ..

2.7.s:
śrotriyāśca dvijāḥ sarve daridrāḥ syuḥ kalau yuge ..
viṣṇubhaktirnarāṇāṃ tu prāyaśo naiva vartate ..41..
prāyaḥ pākhaṃḍabhūyiṣṭhaṃ puṇyakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati ..
śūdrā dharmapravaktāro jaṭilāstāpasāḥ kalau ..42..
sarve cālpāyuṣo martyā dayāhīnā śaṭhā janāḥ ..
sarve dharmapravaktāraḥ sarve ca grahaṇotsavāḥ .. 43 ..
svārcanaṃ cā'pi hīcchaṃti vṛthā nindāparāyaṇāḥ ..
asūyāniratāḥ sarve prabhoḥ svagṛhamāgate .. 44 ..
bhrātā ca bhaginīgaṃtā pitā putrīṃ ca vai kalau ..
sarve'pi śūdrīniratāḥ sarve vārāṃganāratāḥ .. 45 ..

vyaktīkurvaṃti sādhūnāṃ doṣamekaṃ durāgrahāḥ .. 46 ..

2.7.d:
श्रोत्रियाश्च द्विजाः सर्वे दरिद्राः स्युः कलौ युगे ..
विष्णुभक्तिर्नराणां तु प्रायशो नैव वर्तते ..41..
प्रायः पाखंडभूयिष्ठं पुण्यक्षेत्रं भविष्यति ..
शूद्रा धर्मप्रवक्तारो जटिलास्तापसाः कलौ ..42..
सर्वे चाल्पायुषो मर्त्या दयाहीना शठा जनाः ..
सर्वे धर्मप्रवक्तारः सर्वे च ग्रहणोत्सवाः .. 43 ..
स्वार्चनं चाऽपि हीच्छंति वृथा निन्दापरायणाः ..
असूयानिरताः सर्वे प्रभोः स्वगृहमागते .. 44 ..
भ्राता च भगिनीगंता पिता पुत्रीं च वै कलौ ..
सर्वेऽपि शूद्रीनिरताः सर्वे वारांगनारताः .. 45 ..
साधून्नैव विजानंति बहुपापांश्च मन्यते ..
व्यक्तीकुर्वंति साधूनां दोषमेकं दुराग्रहाः .. 46 ..
पापानां दोषजातानि गुणत्वेन वदन्ति हि ..
दोषमेव प्रगृह्णंति कलौ तु विगुणा जनाः ..47..
जलौका धर्मसंयुक्ता रक्तं पिवति नो पयः ..

2.7.s:
auṣadhyaḥ sattvahīnā hi ṛtūn vyatyayāstathā .. 48 ..

naṭanartakavidyāsu prītimanto narāḥ kalau .. 49 ..
vedavedāṃtavidyāsu niratā ye guṇādhikāḥ ..

tyaktaśrāddhakriyāḥ sarve tyaktavedoditakriyāḥ ..

śṛṃgārarasa nirvāṇāstadgītānyeva te jaguḥ ..51..

tāndṛṣṭvā gharmavarṇo'pi subhīto'tyantavismitaḥ ..

2.7.d:
औषध्यः सत्त्वहीना हि ऋतून् व्यत्ययास्तथा .. 48 ..
दुर्भिक्षं सर्वराष्ट्रेषु कन्या काले न सूयते ..
नटनर्तकविद्यासु प्रीतिमन्तो नराः कलौ .. 49 ..
वेदवेदांतविद्यासु निरता ये गुणाधिकाः ..
भृत्यान्पश्यंति तान्मूढास्ते भ्रष्टाश्चाखिला नृप .. 2.7.22.50 ..
त्यक्तश्राद्धक्रियाः सर्वे त्यक्तवेदोदितक्रियाः ..
जिह्वायां विष्णुनामानि न वर्तंते कदाचन ..
शृंगाररस निर्वाणास्तद्गीतान्येव ते जगुः ..51..
न विष्णुसेवा न च शास्त्रवार्ता न यागदीक्षा न विचारलेशः ..
न तीर्थयात्रा न च दानधर्माः कलौ जने क्वाऽपि बभूव चित्रम् .. 52 ..

वंशं पापात्क्षयं यांतं दृष्ट्वा द्वीपांतरं ययौ .. 53 ..
स चरन्सर्वद्वीपेषु लोकेष्वेव तु सर्वशः ..
पितृलोकं ययौ धीमान्कदाचित्कौतुकान्वितः .. 54 ..

2.7.s:
tatrā'paśyanmahāghorāñcchrāmyamāṇāṃśca karmabhiḥ ..55..
dhāvato rudamānāṃśca patataḥ patitānapi ..
tatrāpaśyaccāndhakūpe patitānsvānpitṝnadhaḥ .. 56 ..
dūrvāgralaṃbino dīnāndūrvācchede hi śaṃkitān ..
tadā prāptaḥ ko'pi cākhurdūrvāmūlaṃ tadāśrayam .. 57 ..
tena bhāgatrayaṃ cāttameko bhāgovaśeṣitaḥ ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā te kṣīyamāṇaṃ mūlaṃ duḥkhena karṣiṇaḥ .. .. 58 ..
adho dṛṣṭvā cāṃ'dhakūpaṃ taṭapātādibhīṣaṇam ..
duruttāraṃ mahāghoraṃ karmaṇāptaṃ suduḥkhitāḥ .. 59 ..
agre cā'pi duruttāramavalaṃbavivarjitam ..
tāndraṣṭvā vismito bhūtvā dayālurvākyamabravīt ..2.7.22.60..
ke yūyaṃ patitā hyasminkena dustarakarmaṇā ..
kasya gotre samutpannāḥ kathaṃ vo muktirūrjitā .. 61 ..
etadyūyaṃ vadadhvaṃ me śarma vo'tha bhaviṣyati ..
ityevamuditāstena pitaro'tha suduḥkhitāḥ .. 62 ..
2.7.d:
तत्राऽपश्यन्महाघोराञ्च्छ्राम्यमाणांश्च कर्मभिः ..55..
धावतो रुदमानांश्च पततः पतितानपि ..
तत्रापश्यच्चान्धकूपे पतितान्स्वान्पितॄनधः .. 56 ..
दूर्वाग्रलंबिनो दीनान्दूर्वाच्छेदे हि शंकितान् ..
तदा प्राप्तः कोऽपि चाखुर्दूर्वामूलं तदाश्रयम् .. 57 ..
तेन भागत्रयं चात्तमेको भागोवशेषितः ..
तं दृष्ट्वा ते क्षीयमाणं मूलं दुःखेन कर्षिणः .. .. 58 ..
अधो दृष्ट्वा चांऽधकूपं तटपातादिभीषणम् ..
दुरुत्तारं महाघोरं कर्मणाप्तं सुदुःखिताः .. 59 ..
अग्रे चाऽपि दुरुत्तारमवलंबविवर्जितम् ..
तान्द्रष्ट्वा विस्मितो भूत्वा दयालुर्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ..2.7.22.60..
के यूयं पतिता ह्यस्मिन्केन दुस्तरकर्मणा ..
कस्य गोत्रे समुत्पन्नाः कथं वो मुक्तिरूर्जिता .. 61 ..
एतद्यूयं वदध्वं मे शर्म वोऽथ भविष्यति ..
इत्येवमुदितास्तेन पितरोऽथ सुदुःखिताः .. 62 ..
2.7.m:
There he saw [beings] extremely terrible, worn out by their deeds,
running, crying out, falling, and already fallen.
There he saw his own ancestors fallen down into a blind well,
wretched, hanging from the tip of a blade of dūrvā grass, trembling at the thought of the dūrvā breaking.
Then a certain rat came upon the root of that dūrvā grass which was their support;
by it three parts were eaten away, and only one part remained.
Seeing that root diminishing, they were tormented with distress.
Looking down, they saw the blind well, terrifying with crumbling edges and the like,
hard to cross, very dreadful, attained by their action, exceedingly miserable.
Ahead too, it was hard to escape, devoid of any support.
Seeing them, the compassionate man, filled with wonder, spoke [these] words:
"Who are you that have fallen into this, by what deed hard to overcome?"
In whose gotra were you born? How can your powerful liberation be attained?
Tell me this; then welfare will come to you."
Addressed in this manner by him, the ancestors, deeply afflicted with sorrow,

2.7.s:
tamūcuḥ karuṇāṃ vācaṃ dharmaśruti puraḥsarāḥ ..
.. pitara ūcuḥ .. ..
vayaṃ śrīvatsagotrīyā bhuvi santānavarjitāḥ .. 63 ..
piṃḍaśrāddhavihīnāśca tena pacyāmahe vayam ..
niḥsantāno'pi no vaṃśo jātaḥ pāpaiḥ kalau yuge ..64..
nā'smākaṃ piṃḍadaścāsti vaṃśe pāpātkṣayaṃ gate..
tenāṃ'dhakūpe patanaṃ nistaṃtūnāṃ durātmanām ..65..
eko hi vartate vaṃśe dharmavarṇo mahāyaśāḥ ..
sa viraktaścaranneko na gārhasthamupeyivān .. 66 ..
taṃtunā tena bibhrāmo dūrvānālāvalaṃbitāḥ ..
nistaṃtutvācca tanmūlamākhuḥ khādati pratyaham .. 67 ..
ekasyaivā'vaśiṣṭatvātkiṃcinnalo'vaśeṣitaḥ ..
ākhunā khādyamānaśca vartate saumya paśyatām .. .. 68 ..
tasya cā''yuḥkṣaye tāta śeṣamākhurhariṣyati ..
paścātkūpe patiṣyāmo duruttāreṃ'dhatāmase .. 69 ..
tasmāttvaṃ ca bhuvaṃ gatvā dharmavarṇaṃ prabodhaya ..
2.7.d:
तमूचुः करुणां वाचं धर्मश्रुति पुरःसराः ..
.. पितर ऊचुः .. ..
वयं श्रीवत्सगोत्रीया भुवि सन्तानवर्जिताः .. 63 ..
पिंडश्राद्धविहीनाश्च तेन पच्यामहे वयम् ..
निःसन्तानोऽपि नो वंशो जातः पापैः कलौ युगे ..64..
नाऽस्माकं पिंडदश्चास्ति वंशे पापात्क्षयं गते..
तेनांऽधकूपे पतनं निस्तंतूनां दुरात्मनाम् ..65..
एको हि वर्तते वंशे धर्मवर्णो महायशाः ..
स विरक्तश्चरन्नेको न गार्हस्थमुपेयिवान् .. 66 ..
तंतुना तेन बिभ्रामो दूर्वानालावलंबिताः ..

2.7.m:
Spoke compassionate words to him, preceded by [teachings of] righteousness and the scriptures:
The ancestors said:
"We belong to the Śrīvatsa gotra, bereft of offspring on earth,
And deprived of rice-ball offerings and śrāddhas; therefore, we are tormented.
Our lineage too has become childless through sins in the Kali age;
We have no one to offer rice-balls, since the lineage has gone to ruin through sin.
Therefore, there is a fall into a blind well for us wicked ones, left without descendants.
Indeed, one alone remains in the lineage, named Dharmavarṇa, of great renown.
Dispassionate, wandering alone, he has not entered upon householdership.
Supported by him as our thread, we hang suspended by a reed of dūrvā grass.
Because there are no other threads, a rat daily gnaws at its root.
Since only one [descendant] remains, a little of the reed is left;
And it is being eaten away by the rat, gentle one, as we look on.
When his lifespan ends, dear one, the rat will devour the rest;
Afterwards we will fall into the blind, dark well from which it is hard to cross.
Therefore, go to earth and awaken Dharmavarṇa,

2.7.m:
The sage averse to householdership, with our words that evoke compassion:
'Your ancestors, intensely afflicted, have fallen into hell,
Seen by me in a blind, impassable well, hanging from a dūrvā reed.
That dūrvā reed has the form of the lineage, O sage, and constantly at its root,
A rat named Time daily gnaws its base.
By the destruction of the lineage in succession, you alone are left behind.
By this, O sage, three quarters of the root of the dūrvā are destroyed.
One part remains here, because you exist on earth.
The rat indeed nibbles at you slightly, in the gradual diminution of your life.
When you have passed away, our fall and yours as well will take place
Into the very well of blinding darkness, when the lineage is fully extinct.
Therefore, taking up householdership, bring about the growth of descendants.
Thereby our higher realm and yours too will come to be, without doubt.
Many sons should be desired, in case even one might go to Gayā,
Or perform a horse sacrifice, or release a dark blue bull;

2.7.m:
Or if even one, in the month of Vaiśākha, Māgha, or Kārtika,
Will perform ritual ablution, śrāddha, and donation on our behalf;
By that, an upward path and rescue from hell would come to us.
Or let one be a devotee of Viṣṇu, or let one observe the day of Hari,
Or let one listen to the story of Viṣṇu that destroys sin:
His past hundred generations and a future hundred generations as well,
Even if surrounded by sin, never see hell anywhere.
What is the use of other numerous sons who are devoid of compassion and virtue,
Who, when born into a family, do not truly worship Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa?
For there is no heavenly world for one without a son; people know all this.
Even there, such offspring endowed with compassion is rare.'
Having thus awakened him with these truthful words,
Direct the mind of him, dispassionate and chaste, toward householdership."
Hearing the words of the ancestors, Dharmavarṇa was greatly astonished.
Bowing with folded hands, weeping and trembling, he spoke:

2.7.m:
"I am Dharmavarṇa by name, born of your lineage, stubborn in purpose.
Having heard the words of the great-souled Nārada at the sacrifice:
'No one possesses control of the tongue or control of the genitals in the Kali age';
And seeing those most sinful people on earth, filled with doubt,
Afraid of association with wicked people, I have lived wandering among other islands.
Three quarters of this Kali age have passed, and even in this final quarter,
Three and a half portions have gone by now, O forefathers.
I did not know your suffering; my life has passed in vain,
Since in the lineage in which I was born, I have not removed the debt to my parents.
What is the use of him who is merely born as a burden to the earth, an enemy here,
Who, having been born, does not worship Viṣṇu, the ancestors, the gods, and the seers?"
"I will carry out your command; command me on earth,
so that there will be no affliction from the Kali [age] there, or from worldly existence either.
The duties too must be performed by me, your son, on the earth's surface."
Having been spoken to in this way by that descendant, the wise Dharmavarṇa,

2.7.m:
their minds somewhat comforted, O king, they said this:
"Son, behold this state of your noble ancestors,
falling due to lack of progeny, hanging on merely to a blade of dūrvā grass.
Take up the householder's life and deliver us through offspring!
Those who delight in narratives of Viṣṇu, who remember Hari day and night,
and who are devoted to right conduct—Kali indeed does not afflict them.
He in whose house a śālagrāma stone remains, O honour-giver,
or in whose home the Mahābhārata [is kept]—Kali indeed does not afflict him.
And he who is devoted to [the observances of] Vaiśākha, and intent on the ritual ablution of Māgha,
and he who gives a lamp in Kārtika—Kali indeed does not afflict him.
And whoever listens daily to the narrative of noble Viṣṇu,
which destroys sin and grants liberation, which is divine—Kali indeed does not afflict him.
In whose house the Vaiśvadeva [offering is made], and in whose house the auspicious tulasī [stands],
and in whose courtyard there is an auspicious cow—Kali indeed does not afflict him.
Therefore, there is no fear here, even in an age whose nature is sin.

2.7.m:
Go quickly to the earth, son; this month is named Mādhava (Vaiśākha).
For the benefit of all, when the sun is stationed in Aries,
all thirty lunar days are meritorious when the sun is stationed in Aries.
The merit acquired on each single one is multiplied ten millionfold.
Even there, the new-moon day of the dark fortnight of Caitra grants liberation to men.
It is dear to the ancestors and gods, bestowing immediate liberation.
Those who perform a śrāddha dedicated to the ancestors on that day,
along with a water-pot and an offering of piṇḍas, obtain an inexhaustible fruit.
And those who perform a śrāddha on the new moon in spring (Madhu), O son,
a śrāddha performed by them in the sacred field of Gayā becomes ten million times greater.
If one performs a śrāddha on the new moon in spring, even with mere vegetables,
ten million śrāddhas are performed by him at Gayā, without doubt.
